¬ (∃ C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit,
    PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C ∧ C.size ≤ 11 ∧
    (∀ x : Fin 9 → Bool, C.eval (List.ofFn x) = ((x 0 && x 4 && x 8) || (x 0 && x 5 && x 7) || (x 1 && x 3 && x 8) || (x 1 && x 5 && x 6) || (x 2 && x 3 && x 7) || (x 2 && x 4 && x 6))) ∧
    C.output + 1 = 9 + C.size ∧
    (∀ j : Fin C.gates.length,
      ((C.gates.get j).op = PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.not ∧
          ∃ a, a < 9 + j.val ∧ (C.gates.get j).inputs = [a]) ∨
      (((C.gates.get j).op = PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.and ∨
          (C.gates.get j).op = PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.or) ∧
          ∃ a b, a < b ∧ b < 9 + j.val ∧ (C.gates.get j).inputs = [a, b])) ∧
    (∀ j : Fin C.gates.length,
      (∃ x y : Fin 9 → Bool,
        (C.wires (List.ofFn x)).getD (9 + j.val) false ≠ (C.wires (List.ofFn y)).getD (9 + j.val) false) ∧
      ∀ k, k < 9 + j.val → ∃ x : Fin 9 → Bool,
        (C.wires (List.ofFn x)).getD (9 + j.val) false ≠ (C.wires (List.ofFn x)).getD k false) ∧
    (∀ j : Fin C.gates.length, j.val + 1 < C.gates.length →
      ∃ k : Fin C.gates.length, j.val < k.val ∧ 9 + j.val ∈ (C.gates.get k).inputs) ∧
    C.gates.head? = some ⟨PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.and, [0, 4]⟩ ∧
    C.gates.tail.head? = some ⟨PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.and, [1, 2]⟩)
changed.sketch: A proof is one explicit counterexample to the positive statement L-meta-27171; none is expected if that statement is true.

∃ C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit,
    PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C ∧ C.size ≤ 11 ∧
    (∀ x : Fin 9 → Bool, C.eval (List.ofFn x) = ((x 0 && x 4 && x 8) || (x 0 && x 5 && x 7) || (x 1 && x 3 && x 8) || (x 1 && x 5 && x 6) || (x 2 && x 3 && x 7) || (x 2 && x 4 && x 6))) ∧
    C.output + 1 = 9 + C.size ∧
    (∀ j : Fin C.gates.length,
      ((C.gates.get j).op = PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.not ∧
          ∃ a, a < 9 + j.val ∧ (C.gates.get j).inputs = [a]) ∨
      (((C.gates.get j).op = PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.and ∨
          (C.gates.get j).op = PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.or) ∧
          ∃ a b, a < b ∧ b < 9 + j.val ∧ (C.gates.get j).inputs = [a, b])) ∧
    (∀ j : Fin C.gates.length,
      (∃ x y : Fin 9 → Bool,
        (C.wires (List.ofFn x)).getD (9 + j.val) false ≠ (C.wires (List.ofFn y)).getD (9 + j.val) false) ∧
      ∀ k, k < 9 + j.val → ∃ x : Fin 9 → Bool,
        (C.wires (List.ofFn x)).getD (9 + j.val) false ≠ (C.wires (List.ofFn x)).getD k false) ∧
    (∀ j : Fin C.gates.length, j.val + 1 < C.gates.length →
      ∃ k : Fin C.gates.length, j.val < k.val ∧ 9 + j.val ∈ (C.gates.get k).inputs) ∧
    C.gates.head? = some ⟨PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.and, [0, 4]⟩ ∧
    C.gates.tail.head? = some ⟨PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.and, [2, 6]⟩
changed.unlocks: One case of the cut of 3 by 3 perfect matching at 11 gates by its two earliest gates: with the other cases under the same earliest gate and their cover, the floor for that earliest gate, one of five the assembly takes.
changed.sketch: The two earliest gates are written out and the circuit is in normal form: output last, operands increasing, no constant or repeated wire, every gate but the last listed later. For the no side these are hypotheses: split on the third gate, or write the normal-form gate lists of at most 11 gates with these two gates as clauses and replay a solver certificate inside Lean (the checker takes no native_decide). For the some side: one explicit gate list, each clause by decide over the 512 inputs. Too large for one file? Hand it back and it is cut again by its next gate.

∃ C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit,
    PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C ∧ C.size ≤ 11 ∧
    (∀ x : Fin 9 → Bool, C.eval (List.ofFn x) = ((x 0 && x 4 && x 8) || (x 0 && x 5 && x 7) || (x 1 && x 3 && x 8) || (x 1 && x 5 && x 6) || (x 2 && x 3 && x 7) || (x 2 && x 4 && x 6))) ∧
    C.output + 1 = 9 + C.size ∧
    (∀ j : Fin C.gates.length,
      ((C.gates.get j).op = PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.not ∧
          ∃ a, a < 9 + j.val ∧ (C.gates.get j).inputs = [a]) ∨
      (((C.gates.get j).op = PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.and ∨
          (C.gates.get j).op = PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.or) ∧
          ∃ a b, a < b ∧ b < 9 + j.val ∧ (C.gates.get j).inputs = [a, b])) ∧
    (∀ j : Fin C.gates.length,
      (∃ x y : Fin 9 → Bool,
        (C.wires (List.ofFn x)).getD (9 + j.val) false ≠ (C.wires (List.ofFn y)).getD (9 + j.val) false) ∧
      ∀ k, k < 9 + j.val → ∃ x : Fin 9 → Bool,
        (C.wires (List.ofFn x)).getD (9 + j.val) false ≠ (C.wires (List.ofFn x)).getD k false) ∧
    (∀ j : Fin C.gates.length, j.val + 1 < C.gates.length →
      ∃ k : Fin C.gates.length, j.val < k.val ∧ 9 + j.val ∈ (C.gates.get k).inputs) ∧
    C.gates.head? = some ⟨PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.and, [0, 1]⟩ ∧
    C.gates.tail.head? = some ⟨PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.or, [3, 7]⟩
changed.unlocks: One case of the cut of 3 by 3 perfect matching at 11 gates by its two earliest gates: with the other cases under the same earliest gate and their cover, the floor for that earliest gate, one of five the assembly takes.
changed.sketch: The two earliest gates are written out and the circuit is in normal form: output last, operands increasing, no constant or repeated wire, every gate but the last listed later. For the no side these are hypotheses: split on the third gate, or write the normal-form gate lists of at most 11 gates with these two gates as clauses and replay a solver certificate inside Lean (the checker takes no native_decide). For the some side: one explicit gate list, each clause by decide over the 512 inputs. Too large for one file? Hand it back and it is cut again by its next gate.

∃ C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit,
    PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C ∧ C.size ≤ 12 ∧
    (∀ x : Fin 9 → Bool, C.eval (List.ofFn x) = ((x 0 && x 4 && x 8) || (x 0 && x 5 && x 7) || (x 1 && x 3 && x 8) || (x 1 && x 5 && x 6) || (x 2 && x 3 && x 7) || (x 2 && x 4 && x 6))) ∧
    C.output + 1 = 9 + C.size ∧
    (∀ j : Fin C.gates.length,
      ((C.gates.get j).op = PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.not ∧
          ∃ a, a < 9 + j.val ∧ (C.gates.get j).inputs = [a]) ∨
      (((C.gates.get j).op = PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.and ∨
          (C.gates.get j).op = PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.or) ∧
          ∃ a b, a < b ∧ b < 9 + j.val ∧ (C.gates.get j).inputs = [a, b])) ∧
    (∀ j : Fin C.gates.length,
      (∃ x y : Fin 9 → Bool,
        (C.wires (List.ofFn x)).getD (9 + j.val) false ≠ (C.wires (List.ofFn y)).getD (9 + j.val) false) ∧
      ∀ k, k < 9 + j.val → ∃ x : Fin 9 → Bool,
        (C.wires (List.ofFn x)).getD (9 + j.val) false ≠ (C.wires (List.ofFn x)).getD k false) ∧
    (∀ j : Fin C.gates.length, j.val + 1 < C.gates.length →
      ∃ k : Fin C.gates.length, j.val < k.val ∧ 9 + j.val ∈ (C.gates.get k).inputs) ∧
    C.gates.head? = some ⟨PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.and, [0, 4]⟩ ∧
    C.gates.tail.head? = some ⟨PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.and, [1, 8]⟩
changed.unlocks: One case of the cut of 3 by 3 perfect matching at 12 gates by its two earliest gates: with the other cases under the same earliest gate and their cover, the floor for that earliest gate, one of five the assembly takes.
changed.sketch: The two earliest gates are written out and the circuit is in normal form: output last, operands increasing, no constant or repeated wire, every gate but the last listed later. For the no side these are hypotheses: split on the third gate, or write the normal-form gate lists of at most 12 gates with these two gates as clauses and replay a solver certificate inside Lean (the checker takes no native_decide). For the some side: one explicit gate list, each clause by decide over the 512 inputs. Too large for one file? Hand it back and it is cut again by its next gate.

changed.title: A ternary CNF propagates every forced bit of the two scheduled words, their two names and their common key
changed.statement:
∀ (k r : ℕ), 0 < k →
  let rot := fun (s word : Nat) =>
    ((word <<< (s % k)) ||| (word >>> (k - s % k))) % 2 ^ k
  let step := fun (word : Nat) =>
    (List.range k).foldl (fun acc i =>
      acc ||| ((xor (word.testBit i)
        (!(word.testBit ((i + 1) % k)) && word.testBit ((i + 2) % k))).toNat <<< i)) 0
  let constant := fun (j : Nat) => 3 ^ (k + j) % 2 ^ k
  let first := fun (rowKey rowName : Nat) =>
    (List.range r).foldl (fun rowState rowIndex =>
      step (rowState ^^^ rot 1 rowState ^^^ rot (k - 1) rowState) ^^^
        rot (2 * rowIndex) rowKey ^^^ constant (rowIndex + 1)) (rot 1 rowKey ^^^ rowName)
  let second := fun (colKey colName : Nat) =>
    (List.range r).foldl (fun colState colIndex =>
      step (colState ^^^ rot 2 colState ^^^ rot (k - 2) colState) ^^^
        rot (3 * (colIndex + 1) + 1) colKey ^^^ constant (r + (colIndex + 1)))
      (rot 3 colKey ^^^ colName)
  let V := Fin 5 × Fin k
  let word := fun (v : V → Bool) (track : Fin 5) =>
    ∑ j : Fin k, (v (track,j)).toNat * 2^j.val
  let agrees := fun (v : V → Bool) =>
    word v 3 = first (word v 2) (word v 0) ∧
    word v 4 = second (word v 2) (word v 1)
  let B := 17*r+3
  let rounds := 2*(B+1)*(Nat.clog 2 k) + B+16
  ∃ (m : ℕ) (F : Finset (PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause (Sum V (Fin m)))),
    m + (∑ C ∈ F, C.card) ≤ 256*(k+1)*2^(3*B) ∧
    (∀ C ∈ F, C.card ≤ 3) ∧
    (∀ v : V → Bool, agrees v ↔ ∃ aux : Fin m → Bool,
      PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Satisfies (Sum.elim v aux) (↑F : Set _)) ∧
    ∀ ρ : V → Option Bool,
      let seed : Set (PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Literal (Sum V (Fin m))) :=
        {l | ∃ raw : V, l.1 = Sum.inl raw ∧ ρ raw = some l.2}
      let advance := fun S : Set (PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Literal (Sum V (Fin m))) =>
        S ∪ {l | ∃ C ∈ F, l ∈ C ∧ ∀ other ∈ C, other ≠ l →
          PEqualNP.Search.negLit other ∈ S}
      let known := (advance^[rounds]) seed
      let complete := fun v : V → Bool => agrees v ∧
        ∀ (raw : V) (sign : Bool), ρ raw = some sign → v raw = sign
      ((¬ ∃ v, complete v) ↔ ∃ C ∈ F, ∀ l ∈ C, PEqualNP.Search.negLit l ∈ known) ∧
      ((∃ v, complete v) → ∀ raw : V, ∀ sign : Bool,
        (∀ v, complete v → v raw = sign) ↔ (Sum.inl raw, sign) ∈ known)

changed.title: Two matched Hamming checks admit a polynomial read order and three can force exponential width in every order
changed.statement:
let data := fun (n r : ℕ) (M : Fin r → Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) (S : Finset (Bool × Fin n)) =>
  let V := Bool × Fin n
  let mate := fun (j : Fin r) (v : V) =>
    if v.1 then (false, (M j).symm v.2) else (true, M j v.2)
  let border := S.filter (fun v => ∃ j : Fin r, mate j v ∉ S)
  let rows := fun (x z : V → Bool) (j : Fin r) =>
    let word := fun v : V => if v ∈ S then x v else z v
    let D := (Finset.univ.filter (fun i : Fin n => word (false,i) ≠ word (true,M j i))).card
    decide (16 * Nat.dist (2*D) n ≤ n)
  (border.card, (Finset.univ.image rows).card)
(∀ (n r : ℕ), 32 ≤ n → ∀ (M : Fin r → Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) (S : Finset (Bool × Fin n)),
  let q := data n r M S
  2^q.1 ≤ (2*q.2)^r ∧ q.2 ≤ (n+1)^r * 2^q.1) ∧
(∀ n : ℕ, 32 ≤ n → ∀ M : Fin 2 → Equiv.Perm (Fin n),
  ∃ order : (Bool × Fin n) ≃ Fin (2*n), ∀ t : ℕ,
    (data n 2 M (Finset.univ.filter (fun v => (order v).val < t))).2 ≤ 4*(n+1)^2) ∧
(∃ N : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, N ≤ n → ∃ M : Fin 3 → Equiv.Perm (Fin n),
  ∀ S : Finset (Bool × Fin n), S.card = n → 2^(n/16384) ≤ (data n 3 M S).2)

changed.context: Store completed mismatch counts and the read bits with an unread mate. Each border bit splits a pair in some matching. For three, fix a spanning alternating cycle and choose the third permutation uniformly. A balanced cut with small border has few cycle transitions. changed.title: A signed relation closed on affordable triples characterizes resolution width for unequal parity blocks
changed.statement:
∀ (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) (w : Fin n → ℕ), (∀ i, 0 < w i) →
  let Raw := (i : Fin n) × Fin (w i)
  let parity := fun (y : Raw → Bool) (i : Fin n) =>
    decide (Odd ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin (w i))).filter (fun j => y ⟨i,j⟩ = true)).card)
  let liftAx := fun (F : Set (PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause (Fin n)))
      (A : PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause Raw) =>
    ∃ C ∈ F, ∃ y : Raw → Bool, (∀ lit ∈ C, parity y lit.1 ≠ lit.2) ∧
      A = ((Finset.univ : Finset Raw).filter (fun b => b.1 ∈ C.image Prod.fst)).image
        (fun b => (b, !(y b)))
  let shape := fun (N J : Finset (List Bool)) =>
    [] ∈ N ∧ J ⊆ N ∧
    (∀ (p : List Bool) (b : Bool), p ++ [b] ∈ N → p ∈ J) ∧
    ∀ p ∈ J, p ++ [false] ∈ N ∧ p ++ [true] ∈ N
  let small := fun (F : Set (PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause (Fin n))) (W : ℕ) =>
    ∃ (N J : Finset (List Bool)) (line : List Bool → PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause Raw),
      shape N J ∧ line [] = ∅ ∧ (∀ p ∈ N, (line p).card ≤ W) ∧
      (∀ p ∈ N \ J, liftAx F (line p)) ∧
      ∀ p ∈ J, PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.IsResolvent
        (line (p ++ [false])) (line (p ++ [true])) (line p)
  ∀ (E : Fin n → Fin n → Bool → Prop), (∀ u v s, E u v s → E v u s) →
    let F : Set (PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause (Fin n)) := {C |
      ∃ u v s a, E u v s ∧ C = {(u,!a),(v,a ^^ s)}}
    ∀ W : ℕ,
      Iff (¬ small F W)
        (∃ R : Fin n → Fin n → Bool → Prop,
          (∀ i j s, E i j s → (if i = j then w i else w i + w j) ≤ W → R i j s) ∧
          (∀ i j s, R i j s → R j i s) ∧ (∀ i, ¬ R i i true) ∧
          (∀ i j s t, R i j s → R i j t → s = t) ∧
          ∀ i j k s t, i ≠ j → j ≠ k → i ≠ k → w i + w j + w k ≤ W+1 →
            R i j s → R j k t → R i k (s ^^ t))

When one block completes, two conflicting parity demands would compose on an affordable triple, contradicting the invariant. Follow a width-W proof backwards.

changed.title: Three matched central Hamming checks require exponentially many accepting rectangles across every middle-sized cut
changed.statement:
∃ N : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, N ≤ n →
  let V := Bool × Fin n

changed.title: One monotone circuit excludes incompatible bit values for every syndrome of a binary matrix under arbitrary partial pins
changed.statement:
∀ (n h : ℕ) (A : Fin h → Fin n → ZMod 2),
  let V := Fin n × Bool
  let S := Fin h → ZMod 2
  let compatible := fun (ρ : Fin n → Option Bool) (s : S) (x : Fin n → Bool) =>
    (∀ i b, ρ i = some b → x i = b) ∧
    ∀ j, (∑ i : Fin n, if x i then A j i else 0) = s j
  let pins := fun (ρ : Fin n → Option Bool) =>
    [false, true] ++ List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => decide (ρ i = some false)) ++
      List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => decide (ρ i = some true))
  let Gate := Bool × ℕ × ℕ
  let run := fun (G : List Gate) (ρ : Fin n → Option Bool) =>
    G.foldl (fun (w : List Bool) g =>
      let l := w.getD g.2.1 false
      let r := w.getD g.2.2 false
      w ++ [if g.1 then l && r else l || r]) (pins ρ)
  let depths := fun (G : List Gate) =>
    G.foldl (fun (w : List ℕ) g =>
      w ++ [max (w.getD g.2.1 0) (w.getD g.2.2 0) + 1]) (List.replicate (2+2*n) 0)
  ∃ (G : List Gate) (dead : S → ℕ) (excludeBit : S → V → ℕ),
    G.length ≤ 256*(n+1)*(h+1)*2^h ∧
    (∀ (i : Fin G.length), (G.get i).2.1 < 2+2*n+i.val ∧ (G.get i).2.2 < 2+2*n+i.val) ∧
    ∀ s : S,
      dead s < 2+2*n+G.length ∧ (depths G).getD (dead s) 0 ≤ 16*(h+Nat.clog 2 (n+1)+1) ∧
      (∀ v : V, excludeBit s v < 2+2*n+G.length ∧
        (depths G).getD (excludeBit s v) 0 ≤ 16*(h+Nat.clog 2 (n+1)+1)) ∧
      ∀ ρ : Fin n → Option Bool,

changed.title: Few missing circuit inputs suffice for complete ternary unit propagation with single-exponential dependence on their number
changed.statement:
∀ (n t h : ℕ) (gates : List PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.BinaryGate) (out : Fin t → ℕ),
  let V := Fin n ⊕ Fin t
  let circuit : PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.BinaryCircuit := ⟨gates, 0⟩
  let agrees := fun (v : V → Bool) =>
    let wires := circuit.wires (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => v (Sum.inl i)))
    ∀ j : Fin t, v (Sum.inr j) = wires.getD (out j) false
  let depths := gates.foldl (fun (w : List ℕ) g =>
    w ++ [max (w.getD g.left 0) (w.getD g.right 0) + 1]) (List.replicate n 0)
  let D := (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin t)).sup (fun j => depths.getD (out j) 0)
  let rounds := 128*(D+h+Nat.clog 2 (n+t+1)+1)
  ∃ (m : ℕ) (F : Finset (PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause (Sum V (Fin m)))),
    m + (∑ C ∈ F, C.card) ≤ 262144*(n+t+gates.length+1)*(h+1)^2*(Nat.clog 2 (n+1)+1)*2^h ∧
    (∀ C ∈ F, C.card ≤ 3) ∧
    (∀ v : V → Bool, agrees v ↔ ∃ aux : Fin m → Bool,
      PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Satisfies (Sum.elim v aux) (↑F : Set _)) ∧
    ∀ ρ : V → Option Bool,
      (Finset.univ.filter (fun i : Fin n => ρ (Sum.inl i) = none)).card ≤ h →
      let seed : Set (PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Literal (Sum V (Fin m))) :=
        {l | ∃ raw : V, l.1 = Sum.inl raw ∧ ρ raw = some l.2}
      let advance := fun S : Set (PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Literal (Sum V (Fin m))) =>
        S ∪ {l | ∃ C ∈ F, l ∈ C ∧ ∀ other ∈ C, other ≠ l →
          PEqualNP.Search.negLit other ∈ S}
      let known := (advance^[rounds]) seed
      let complete := fun v : V → Bool => agrees v ∧
        ∀ (raw : V) (sign : Bool), ρ raw = some sign → v raw = sign
      ((¬ ∃ v, complete v) ↔ ∃ C ∈ F, ∀ l ∈ C, PEqualNP.Search.negLit l ∈ known) ∧
      ((∃ v, complete v) → ∀ raw : V, ∀ sign : Bool,
        (∀ v, complete v → v raw = sign) ↔ (Sum.inl raw, sign) ∈ known)

changed.title: The scheduled common-key rule propagates mixed endpoint observations with an arbitrary set of erased driving bits
changed.statement:
∀ (k r h : ℕ), k % 2 = 1 →
  let rot := fun (s word : Nat) =>
    ((word <<< (s % k)) ||| (word >>> (k - s % k))) % 2 ^ k
  let step := fun (word : Nat) =>
    (List.range k).foldl (fun acc i =>
      acc ||| ((xor (word.testBit i)
        (!(word.testBit ((i + 1) % k)) && word.testBit ((i + 2) % k))).toNat <<< i)) 0
  let constant := fun (j : Nat) => 3 ^ (k + j) % 2 ^ k
  let first := fun (rowKey rowName : Nat) =>
    (List.range r).foldl (fun rowState rowIndex =>
      step (rowState ^^^ rot 1 rowState ^^^ rot (k - 1) rowState) ^^^
        rot (2 * rowIndex) rowKey ^^^ constant (rowIndex + 1)) (rot 1 rowKey ^^^ rowName)
  let second := fun (colKey colName : Nat) =>
    (List.range r).foldl (fun colState colIndex =>
      step (colState ^^^ rot 2 colState ^^^ rot (k - 2) colState) ^^^
        rot (3 * (colIndex + 1) + 1) colKey ^^^ constant (r + (colIndex + 1)))
      (rot 3 colKey ^^^ colName)
  let V := Fin 5 × Fin k
  let word := fun (v : V → Bool) (track : Fin 5) =>
    ∑ j : Fin k, (v (track,j)).toNat * 2^j.val
  let agrees := fun (v : V → Bool) =>
    word v 3 = first (word v 2) (word v 0) ∧
    word v 4 = second (word v 2) (word v 1)
  let branch := if k % 3 = 0 then 4^r else 1
  let rounds := 512*((r+1)*(Nat.clog 2 (k+1)+1)+h+1)
  ∃ (m : ℕ) (F : Finset (PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause (Sum V (Fin m)))),
    m + (∑ C ∈ F, C.card) ≤ 16777216*(k+1)*(r+1)*branch*(h+1)^2*(Nat.clog 2 (3*k+1)+1)*2^h ∧
    (∀ C ∈ F, C.card ≤ 3) ∧
    (∀ v : V → Bool, agrees v ↔ ∃ aux : Fin m → Bool,
      PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Satisfies (Sum.elim v aux) (↑F : Set _)) ∧
    ∀ (rowRev colRev : Bool) (ρ : V → Option Bool),
      let driver := fun j : V => j.1 = 2 ∨
        j.1 = (if rowRev then 3 else 0) ∨ j.1 = (if colRev then 4 else 1)
      (Finset.univ.filter (fun j : V => driver j ∧ ρ j = none)).card ≤ h →
      let seed : Set (PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Literal (Sum V (Fin m))) :=
        {l | ∃ raw : V, l.1 = Sum.inl raw ∧ ρ raw = some l.2}
      let advance := fun S : Set (PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Literal (Sum V (Fin m))) =>
        S ∪ {l | ∃ C ∈ F, l ∈ C ∧ ∀ other ∈ C, other ≠ l →
          PEqualNP.Search.negLit other ∈ S}
      let known := (advance^[rounds]) seed
      let complete := fun v : V → Bool => agrees v ∧
        ∀ (raw : V) (sign : Bool), ρ raw = some sign → v raw = sign
      ((¬ ∃ v, complete v) ↔ ∃ C ∈ F, ∀ l ∈ C, PEqualNP.Search.negLit l ∈ known) ∧
      ((∃ v, complete v) → ∀ raw : V, ∀ sign : Bool,
        (∀ v, complete v → v raw = sign) ↔ (Sum.inl raw, sign) ∈ known)

changed.title: An ordered interval recurrence gives the exact height and leaf budgets of resolution on parity-substituted implication paths
changed.statement:
∀ (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) (w : Fin n → ℕ), (∀ i, 0 < w i) →
  let Raw := (i : Fin n) × Fin (w i)
  let parity := fun (y : Raw → Bool) (i : Fin n) =>
    decide (Odd ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin (w i))).filter (fun j => y ⟨i,j⟩ = true)).card)
  let liftAx := fun (F : Set (PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause (Fin n)))
      (A : PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause Raw) =>
    ∃ C ∈ F, ∃ y : Raw → Bool, (∀ lit ∈ C, parity y lit.1 ≠ lit.2) ∧
      A = ((Finset.univ : Finset Raw).filter (fun b => b.1 ∈ C.image Prod.fst)).image
        (fun b => (b, !(y b)))
  let shape := fun (N J : Finset (List Bool)) =>
    [] ∈ N ∧ J ⊆ N ∧
    (∀ (p : List Bool) (b : Bool), p ++ [b] ∈ N → p ∈ J) ∧
    ∀ p ∈ J, p ++ [false] ∈ N ∧ p ++ [true] ∈ N
  let refutes := fun (F : Set (PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause (Fin n))) (H K : ℕ) =>
    ∃ (N J : Finset (List Bool)) (line : List Bool → PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause Raw),
      shape N J ∧ line [] = ∅ ∧ (∀ p ∈ N, p.length ≤ H) ∧ (N \ J).card ≤ K ∧
      (∀ p ∈ N \ J, liftAx F (line p)) ∧
      ∀ p ∈ J, PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.IsResolvent
        (line (p ++ [false])) (line (p ++ [true])) (line p)
  let atV := fun i : ℕ => (⟨i % n, Nat.mod_lt _ hn⟩ : Fin n)
  let F : Set (PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause (Fin n)) := {C |
    C = {(atV 0,true)} ∨ C = {(atV (n-1),false)} ∨
      ∃ i : ℕ, i+1 < n ∧ C = {(atV i,false),(atV (i+1),true)}}
  let tab : ℕ → ℕ → ℕ → ℕ → ℕ → Prop := Nat.rec
    (fun i j _ K => i=j ∧ 1≤K)
    (fun _ prev i j H K => (i=j ∧ 1≤K) ∨ ∃ v : Fin n,
      i ≤ v.val ∧ v.val < j ∧ w v ≤ H ∧ ∃ a c : ℕ,
        2^(w v-1)*(a+c) ≤ K ∧ prev i v.val (H-w v) a ∧ prev (v.val+1) j (H-w v) c)
  ∀ H K : ℕ, Iff (refutes F H K) (tab n 0 n H K)

An interior query is a threshold comparison on the remaining interval. Bypass comparisons with a constant answer. Conversely on any word maintain a true left and false right endpoint and follow the indicated inconsistent half. Apply the unequal-width parity tree transfer.

changed.title: Two explicit costs determine all height and leaf budgets on an anchored cycle of parity blocks
changed.statement:
∀ (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) (b : ℕ), 0 < b →
  let w := fun _ : Fin n => b
  let Raw := (i : Fin n) × Fin (w i)
  let parity := fun (y : Raw → Bool) (i : Fin n) =>
    decide (Odd ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin (w i))).filter (fun j => y ⟨i,j⟩ = true)).card)
  let liftAx := fun (F : Set (PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause (Fin n)))
      (A : PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause Raw) =>
    ∃ C ∈ F, ∃ y : Raw → Bool, (∀ lit ∈ C, parity y lit.1 ≠ lit.2) ∧
      A = ((Finset.univ : Finset Raw).filter (fun b => b.1 ∈ C.image Prod.fst)).image
        (fun b => (b, !(y b)))
  let shape := fun (N J : Finset (List Bool)) =>
    [] ∈ N ∧ J ⊆ N ∧
    (∀ (p : List Bool) (b : Bool), p ++ [b] ∈ N → p ∈ J) ∧
    ∀ p ∈ J, p ++ [false] ∈ N ∧ p ++ [true] ∈ N
  let refutes := fun (F : Set (PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause (Fin n))) (H K : ℕ) =>
    ∃ (N J : Finset (List Bool)) (line : List Bool → PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause Raw),
      shape N J ∧ line [] = ∅ ∧ (∀ p ∈ N, p.length ≤ H) ∧ (N \ J).card ≤ K ∧
      (∀ p ∈ N \ J, liftAx F (line p)) ∧
      ∀ p ∈ J, PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.IsResolvent
        (line (p ++ [false])) (line (p ++ [true])) (line p)
  let base := 2^(b-1)
  let balanced := fun m : ℕ =>
    let d := Nat.clog 2 m
    (2^d-m)*base^(d-1) + (2*m-2^d)*base^d
  let atV := fun i : ℕ => (⟨i % n, Nat.mod_lt _ hn⟩ : Fin n)
  let first := atV 0
  let last := atV (n-1)
  let F : Set (PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause (Fin n)) := {C |
    C = {(last,true),(first,true)} ∨ C = {(last,false),(first,true)} ∨
      C = {(last,false),(first,false)} ∨
    ∃ i : ℕ, i+1 < n ∧ C = {(atV i,false),(atV (i+1),true)}}
  ∀ H K : ℕ, 2 ≤ n →
    Iff (refutes F H K)
      ((b*(1+Nat.clog 2 n) ≤ H ∧ base*(2*base + balanced n) ≤ K) ∨
       (b*Nat.clog 2 (n+3) ≤ H ∧ balanced (n+3) ≤ K))

Search for a descent between sentinels, resolving either end pair by the opposite endpoint. Apply the parity price at every outer leaf.

changed.title: Adding overlapping parity equations with bounded union gives an exact test of ordinary resolution width
changed.statement:
∀ (n : ℕ) (w : Fin n → ℕ), (∀ v, 0 < w v) →
  let Base := PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause (Fin n)
  let can := fun (a : Fin n → ℕ) (F : Set Base) (W : ℕ) =>
    let Raw := (v : Fin n) × Fin (a v)
    let val := fun (x : Raw → Bool) (v : Fin n) =>
      decide (Odd (((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin (a v))).filter (fun j => x ⟨v,j⟩ = true)).card))
    let lifted : Set (PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause Raw) := {A |
      ∃ C ∈ F, ∃ x : Raw → Bool, (∀ l ∈ C, val x l.1 ≠ l.2) ∧
        A = ((Finset.univ : Finset Raw).filter (fun z => z.1 ∈ C.image Prod.fst)).image
          (fun z => (z, !(x z)))}
    ∃ π : List (PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause Raw),
      PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.IsRefutation lifted π ∧ ∀ C ∈ π, C.card ≤ W
  let Row := Finset (Fin n) × Bool
  ∀ E : Set Row,
    let F : Set Base := {C | ∃ z ∈ E, ∃ x : Fin n → Bool,
      decide (Odd ((z.1.filter (fun i => x i = true)).card)) ≠ z.2 ∧
      C = z.1.image (fun i => (i, !(x i)))}
    ∀ W : ℕ, Iff (can w F W)
      (∀ R : Set Row,
        (∀ z ∈ E, z.1.sum w ≤ W → z ∈ R) →
        (∀ p ∈ R, ∀ q ∈ R, (p.1 ∩ q.1).Nonempty → (p.1 ∪ q.1).sum w ≤ W+1 →
          ((p.1 \ q.1) ∪ (q.1 \ p.1), p.2 ^^ q.2) ∈ R) →
        ((∅ : Finset (Fin n)), true) ∈ R)

Two conflicting demands for the last bit of a block would add to a violated row on the other complete blocks. The contradictory empty equation ends the argument.

changed.title: One base resolution tree is width-optimal throughout sufficiently large unequal linear growth of private parity blocks
changed.statement:
∀ (n : ℕ) (slope offset : Fin n → ℕ), (∀ v, 0 < slope v + offset v) →
  let Base := PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause (Fin n)
  let can := fun (a : Fin n → ℕ) (F : Set Base) (W : ℕ) =>
    let Raw := (v : Fin n) × Fin (a v)
    let val := fun (x : Raw → Bool) (v : Fin n) =>
      decide (Odd (((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin (a v))).filter (fun j => x ⟨v,j⟩ = true)).card))
    let lifted : Set (PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause Raw) := {A |
      ∃ C ∈ F, ∃ x : Raw → Bool, (∀ l ∈ C, val x l.1 ≠ l.2) ∧
        A = ((Finset.univ : Finset Raw).filter (fun z => z.1 ∈ C.image Prod.fst)).image
          (fun z => (z, !(x z)))}
    ∃ π : List (PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause Raw),
      PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.IsRefutation lifted π ∧ ∀ C ∈ π, C.card ≤ W
  let vars := fun (C : Base) => C.image Prod.fst
  let clean := fun (C : Base) => ∀ v, ¬ ((v,true) ∈ C ∧ (v,false) ∈ C)
  let w := fun (t : ℕ) (v : Fin n) => t * slope v + offset v
  let T := (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin n)).sum offset + 1
  ∀ F : Set Base, ¬ PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Satisfiable F →
    ∃ (N J : Finset (List Bool)) (line : List Bool → Base) (d k : ℕ),
      [] ∈ N ∧ J ⊆ N ∧ line [] = ∅ ∧
      (∀ (p : List Bool) (b : Bool), p ++ [b] ∈ N → p ∈ J) ∧
      (∀ p ∈ N, clean (line p)) ∧ (∀ p ∈ N \ J, line p ∈ F) ∧
      (∀ p ∈ J, p ++ [false] ∈ N ∧ p ++ [true] ∈ N ∧
        PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.IsResolvent (line (p ++ [false])) (line (p ++ [true])) (line p)) ∧
      ∀ t : ℕ, T ≤ t → ∀ W : ℕ,
        (can (w t) F W ↔ d + (t-T)*k ≤ W) ∧
        (can (w t) F W ↔
          (∀ p ∈ N \ J, (vars (line p)).sum (w t) ≤ W) ∧
          ∀ p ∈ J, (vars (line (p ++ [false])) ∪ vars (line (p ++ [true]))).sum (w t) ≤ W+1)

changed.title: A monotone circuit counts distinct passing words when a cyclic read admits few words but arbitrarily many paths
changed.statement:
∀ (n q t K : ℕ) (gates : List PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.BinaryGate) (output : Fin t → ℕ),
  let X := Fin n → Bool
  let V := Fin n ⊕ Fin t
  let Edge := Fin n × Fin q × Bool × Fin q
  let P := (V × Bool) ⊕ Edge
  let C : PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.BinaryCircuit := ⟨gates,0⟩
  let dep := gates.foldl (fun (w : List ℕ) g =>
    w ++ [max (w.getD g.left 0) (w.getD g.right 0)+1]) (List.replicate n 0)
  let D := (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin t)).sup (fun j => dep.getD (output j) 0)
  let keyLog := Nat.clog 2 (K+1)
  let budget := 65536*(n+1)*(q+1)^2*(K+1)^2*
    ((n+1)^2*(q+1)^3+gates.length+t+n+(keyLog+1)^2+1)
  let rounds := 64*((n+1)*(Nat.clog 2 (q+1)+1)+D+(keyLog+1)^2+Nat.clog 2 (t+n+2)+1)
  let source := fun (a : P → Bool) =>
    [false,true] ++ List.ofFn (fun j : Fin (Fintype.card P) => a ((Fintype.equivFin P).symm j))
  let Gate := Bool × ℕ × ℕ
  let run := fun (G : List Gate) (a : P → Bool) =>
    G.foldl (fun (w : List Bool) g =>
      let l := w.getD g.2.1 false
      let r := w.getD g.2.2 false
      w ++ [if g.1 then l && r else l || r]) (source a)
  let N := 2 + Fintype.card P
  let depths := fun (G : List Gate) =>
    G.foldl (fun (w : List ℕ) g =>
      w ++ [max (w.getD g.2.1 0) (w.getD g.2.2 0) + 1]) (List.replicate N 0)
  ∃ (G : List Gate) (out : Fin (K+1) → ℕ), G.length ≤ budget ∧
    (∀ i : Fin G.length, (G.get i).2.1 < N+i.val ∧ (G.get i).2.2 < N+i.val) ∧
    (∀ j, out j < N+G.length ∧ (depths G).getD (out j) 0 ≤ rounds) ∧
    ∀ (ρ : V → Option Bool) (blocked : Edge → Bool),
      let bits : P → Bool := Sum.elim (fun p => decide (ρ p.1 = some p.2)) blocked
      let candidates := Finset.univ.filter (fun x : X =>
        (∀ i : Fin n, ∀ b : Bool, ρ (Sum.inl i) = some b → x i = b) ∧
        ∃ path : Fin (n+1) → Fin q, path 0 = path (Fin.last n) ∧
          ∀ i : Fin n, blocked (i,path i.castSucc,x i,path i.succ) = false)
      let accepted := candidates.filter (fun x =>
        ∀ j : Fin t, ∀ b : Bool, ρ (Sum.inr j) = some b →
          (C.wires (List.ofFn x)).getD (output j) false = b)
      (∀ j : Fin (K+1), (run G bits).getD (out j) false = true → accepted.card ≤ j.val) ∧
      (candidates.card ≤ K → ∀ j : Fin (K+1),
        (run G bits).getD (out j) false = true ↔ accepted.card ≤ j.val)
changed.unlocks: It converts few distinct word candidates into sound multiplicity bounds under later circuit observations.
changed.context: Choose binary linear hashes into at most 4(K+1)^2 buckets so each small candidate set is injected by one hash. For each hash scan absent paths to each syndrome, repeating with each bit value prescribed. A bucket is ready if empty or one value is excluded at every site. A ready hash has only singleton or empty buckets. Evaluate gate signs for each bucket, mark failures against output pins, and sort the failure bits to get all count thresholds. Require readiness before reporting. Repeated paths for one word stay in one bucket.

changed.title: A small set of keys surviving early scheduled observations permits monotone exact counting through every later round
changed.statement:
∀ (k r d K : ℕ), 0 < k → d ≤ r →
  let rot := fun (s word : Nat) =>
    ((word <<< (s % k)) ||| (word >>> (k - s % k))) % 2 ^ k
  let step := fun (word : Nat) =>
    (List.range k).foldl (fun acc i =>
      acc ||| ((xor (word.testBit i)
        (!(word.testBit ((i + 1) % k)) && word.testBit ((i + 2) % k))).toNat <<< i)) 0
  let constant := fun (j : Nat) => 3 ^ (k + j) % 2 ^ k
  let first := fun (t rowKey rowName : Nat) =>
    (List.range t).foldl (fun rowState rowIndex =>
      step (rowState ^^^ rot 1 rowState ^^^ rot (k - 1) rowState) ^^^
        rot (2 * rowIndex) rowKey ^^^ constant (rowIndex + 1)) (rot 1 rowKey ^^^ rowName)
  let second := fun (t colKey colName : Nat) =>
    (List.range t).foldl (fun colState colIndex =>
      step (colState ^^^ rot 2 colState ^^^ rot (k - 2) colState) ^^^
        rot (3 * (colIndex + 1) + 1) colKey ^^^ constant (r + (colIndex + 1)))
      (rot 3 colKey ^^^ colName)
  let V := Fin 7 × Fin k
  let P := V × Bool
  let keyLog := Nat.clog 2 (K+1)
  let B := 7*d+3
  let budget := 1048576*(k+1)^2*(K+1)^2*((k+1)*4^B+(r+1)+(keyLog+1)^2)
  let rounds := 128*(k+r+B+(keyLog+1)^2+1)
  let source := fun (a : P → Bool) =>
    [false,true] ++ List.ofFn (fun j : Fin (Fintype.card P) => a ((Fintype.equivFin P).symm j))
  let Gate := Bool × ℕ × ℕ
  let run := fun (G : List Gate) (a : P → Bool) =>
    G.foldl (fun (w : List Bool) g =>
      let l := w.getD g.2.1 false
      let r := w.getD g.2.2 false
      w ++ [if g.1 then l && r else l || r]) (source a)
  let N := 2 + Fintype.card P
  let depths := fun (G : List Gate) =>
    G.foldl (fun (w : List ℕ) g =>
      w ++ [max (w.getD g.2.1 0) (w.getD g.2.2 0) + 1]) (List.replicate N 0)
  ∃ (G : List Gate) (out : Fin (K+1) → ℕ), G.length ≤ budget ∧
    (∀ i : Fin G.length, (G.get i).2.1 < N+i.val ∧ (G.get i).2.2 < N+i.val) ∧
    (∀ j, out j < N+G.length ∧ (depths G).getD (out j) 0 ≤ rounds) ∧
    ∀ (u v : Fin k → Bool) (ρ : V → Option Bool),
      (∀ i, ρ (0,i) = some (u i) ∧ ρ (1,i) = some (v i)) →
      let bits := fun p : P => decide (ρ p.1 = some p.2)
      let word := fun (x : Fin k → Bool) => ∑ j : Fin k, (x j).toNat * 2^j.val
      let fits := fun (track : Fin 7) (x : ℕ) =>
        ∀ i : Fin k, ∀ b : Bool, ρ (track,i) = some b → x.testBit i.val = b
      let candidates := Finset.univ.filter (fun x : Fin k → Bool =>
        fits 2 (word x) ∧ fits 3 (first d (word x) (word u)) ∧
        fits 4 (second d (word x) (word v)))
      let accepted := candidates.filter (fun x =>
        fits 5 (first r (word x) (word u)) ∧ fits 6 (second r (word x) (word v)))
      (∀ j : Fin (K+1), (run G bits).getD (out j) false = true → accepted.card ≤ j.val) ∧
      (candidates.card ≤ K → ∀ j : Fin (K+1),
        (run G bits).getD (out j) false = true ↔ accepted.card ≤ j.val)

changed.title: Every middle cut of three matched central Hamming tests admits literal projections of all intersection thresholds
changed.statement:
∃ N : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, N ≤ n →
  let V := Bool × Fin n
  let q := n / 65536
  let A := Fin q → Bool
  let accepts := fun (M : Fin 3 → Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) (x : V → Bool) =>
    ∀ j : Fin 3,
      let D := (Finset.univ.filter (fun i : Fin n => x (false,i) ≠ x (true,M j i))).card
      16 * Nat.dist (2*D) n ≤ n
  ∃ M : Fin 3 → Equiv.Perm (Fin n), ∀ S : Finset V,
    n ≤ 2*S.card → 2*S.card ≤ 3*n → ∀ k : ℕ, k ≤ q →
    ∃ label : V → Bool ⊕ (Fin q × Bool),
      ∀ a b : A,
        let x := fun v : V => (label v).elim id (fun p =>
          xor p.2 (if v ∈ S then a p.1 else b p.1))
        accepts M x ↔ (Finset.univ.filter (fun i : Fin q => a i = true ∧ b i = true)).card ≤ k

Encode a by (a,a,0) on the read ends and b by (1-b,0,b) on the unread ends. The three distances sum to one plus twice the intersection bit. The target is in its band exactly up to k.

changed.title: Randomized repeated reads of one order for three matched central Hamming tests require a linear product of passes and memory bits
changed.statement:
∃ C N : ℕ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, N ≤ n →
  let V := Bool × Fin n
  let X := V → Bool
  ∃ M : Fin 3 → Equiv.Perm (Fin n),
    let accepts := fun x : X => ∀ j : Fin 3,
      let D := (Finset.univ.filter (fun i : Fin n => x (false,i) ≠ x (true,M j i))).card
      16 * Nat.dist (2*D) n ≤ n
    ∀ (order : Fin (2*n) ≃ V) (p s R : ℕ), 0 < p → 0 < R →
      ∀ (init : Fin R → Fin s)
        (step : Fin R → Fin p → Fin (2*n) → Fin s → Bool → Fin s)
        (out : Fin R → Fin s → Bool),
        let answer := fun (r : Fin R) (x : X) =>
          out r ((List.finRange p).foldl (fun st pass =>
            (List.finRange (2*n)).foldl (fun z j => step r pass j z (x (order j))) st) (init r))
        (∀ x : X, 2*R ≤ 3*(Finset.univ.filter (fun r : Fin R =>
          (answer r x = true ↔ accepts x))).card) →
        n ≤ C*p*Nat.clog 2 s

changed.context: Use the zero-threshold projection at the cut after n reads. Two parties simulate all passes with 2p-1 state messages and one output bit. Embed a coordinate into otherwise disjoint inputs by publicly choosing which side can have a random bit at each other coordinate. Transcript rectangles equate the Hellinger distances of opposite corners. Correctness separates 00 from 11, forcing constant information on the 00 to 10 or 00 to 01 edges. Conditional independence adds the costs over all coordinates. A gate-saving companion cannot exist for a memory bound.

changed.title: A circuit detects bounded closed-walk multiplicity and indexes distinct words in any enabled cyclic binary read
changed.statement:
∃ c : ℕ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ (n q ambiguity : ℕ), 0 < n → 0 < ambiguity →
  let W := Fin n → Bool
  let Edge := Fin n × Fin q × Bool × Fin q
  let Pin := Edge ⊕ (Fin n ⊕ Fin n)
  let N := 2 + Fintype.card Pin
  let D := (Fin (n+1) ⊕ Fin (n+1)) ⊕ (Fin n ⊕ Fin 3)
  let encode := fun (x : W) => ∑ i : Fin n, (x i).toNat * 2^(n-1-i.val)
  let source := fun (enabled : Edge → Bool) (query idx : W) =>
    let input : Pin → Bool := Sum.elim enabled (Sum.elim query idx)
    [false,true] ++ List.ofFn (fun j : Fin (Fintype.card Pin) => input ((Fintype.equivFin Pin).symm j))
  ∃ (G : List PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.BinaryGate) (out : D → ℕ),
    G.length ≤ c*(n+1)^4*(ambiguity+2)^6*(q+1)^(3*(ambiguity+1))*(Nat.clog 2 (q+2)+1)^2 ∧
    (∀ i : Fin G.length, (G.get i).left < N+i.val ∧ (G.get i).right < N+i.val) ∧
    (∀ o, out o < N+G.length) ∧
    ∀ (enabled : Edge → Bool) (query idx : W),
      let paths := fun (x : W) => Finset.univ.filter (fun p : Fin (n+1) → Fin q =>
        p 0 = p (Fin.last n) ∧ ∀ i : Fin n, enabled (i,p i.castSucc,x i,p i.succ) = true)
      let lang := Finset.univ.filter (fun x : W => (paths x).Nonempty)
      let rank := fun (x : W) => (lang.filter (fun y => encode y < encode x)).card
      let index := ∑ i : Fin n, (idx i).toNat * 2^i.val
      let circuit : PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.BinaryCircuit := ⟨G,0⟩
      let bit := fun o => (circuit.wires (source enabled query idx)).getD (out o) false
      let selected : W := fun i => bit (Sum.inr (Sum.inl i))
      let flag := fun (j : Fin 3) => bit (Sum.inr (Sum.inr j))
      (flag 0 = true ↔ ∀ x : W, (paths x).card ≤ ambiguity) ∧
      (flag 0 = true →
        (∀ i : Fin (n+1), bit (Sum.inl (Sum.inl i)) = lang.card.testBit i.val ∧
          bit (Sum.inl (Sum.inr i)) = (rank query).testBit i.val) ∧
        (flag 1 = true ↔ query ∈ lang) ∧ (flag 2 = true ↔ index < lang.card) ∧
        (index < lang.card → selected ∈ lang ∧ rank selected = index) ∧
        (lang.card ≤ index → ∀ i, selected i = false))

changed.title: One doubly stochastic normalization preserves every signed determinant ratio on an arbitrary square matrix
changed.statement:
∀ n : ℕ, 0 < n →
  let I := Fin n
  let S := I × I → Bool
  let P := fun A : Matrix I I ℝ => Matrix.permanent (fun i j => (A i j)^2)
  let Z := fun (A : Matrix I I ℝ) (s : S) =>
    (Matrix.det (fun i j => if s (i,j) then -A i j else A i j : Matrix I I ℝ))^2
  ∀ A : Matrix I I ℝ,
    (∀ s : S, (n.factorial : ℝ) * Z A s ≤ (n : ℝ)^n * P A) ∧
    (0 < P A → ∃ (B : Matrix I I ℝ) (c : ℝ), 0 < c ∧
      (∀ i, (∑ j : I, (B i j)^2) = 1) ∧ (∀ j, (∑ i : I, (B i j)^2) = 1) ∧
      P B = c * P A ∧ (n.factorial : ℝ) ≤ (n : ℝ)^n * P B ∧
      ∀ s : S, Z B s = c * Z A s)
changed.unlocks: Gives the common normalization and uniform range needed for concentration on matrices of arbitrary support.
changed.context: When the permanent of the squared entries vanishes, every permutation product is zero. Otherwise discard entries lying on no nonzero permutation. All signed permutation terms are preserved, and the remaining square-weight board has total support. Apply Sinkhorn-Knopp, taking square roots of the positive row and column scales on the real matrix. All quantities acquire the same factor. Van der Waerden bounds the new permanent below. Hadamard bounds every signed determinant square by one since the rows have norm one.

changed.title: A polynomial-size fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT circuit returns the sign and exponent of a schedule coefficient
changed.statement:
∀ (k r s : Nat) (hk : 0 < k),
  let F := ZMod 2
  let W := Fin k → F
  let ix := fun t : Nat => (⟨t % k, Nat.mod_lt _ hk⟩ : Fin k)
  let rot := fun (amount : Nat) (x : W) (j : Fin k) => x (ix (j.val+k-amount % k))
  let layer := fun (gap : Nat) (x : W) =>
    let m := fun (j : Fin k) => x j + x (ix (j.val+gap)) + x (ix (j.val+k-gap % k))
    fun (j : Fin k) => m j + (1+m (ix (j.val+1))) * m (ix (j.val+2))
  ∀ col : Bool,
    let initial := if col then 3 else 1
    let gap := if col then 2 else 1
    let inject := fun t : Nat => if col then 3*(t+1)+1 else 2*t
    let state := fun (data : W × (Fin r → W)) (key : W) (time : Fin (r+1)) =>
      ((List.finRange r).take time.val).foldl (fun v tick =>
        layer gap v + rot (inject tick.val) key + data.2 tick) (rot initial key + data.1)
    let S := Fin r → W
    let encodeInput := fun (raw : W) (delta : Fin s → W)
      (path : Fin (r+1) → Fin s → W) (test target : W) =>
      let bits := fun (x : W) => (List.finRange k).map (fun j => decide (x j ≠ 0))
      bits raw ++ (List.finRange s).flatMap (fun p => bits (delta p)) ++
      (List.finRange (r+1)).flatMap (fun t =>
        (List.finRange s).flatMap (fun p => bits (path t p))) ++ bits test ++ bits target
    let coords := fun (b : S) => (List.finRange r).flatMap (fun t =>
      (List.finRange k).map (fun j => decide (b t j ≠ 0)))
    let hits := fun (raw : W) (delta : Fin s → W) (path : Fin (r+1) → Fin s → W)
      (test target : W) (c : S) =>
      ((Finset.univ : Finset W).filter (fun name =>
        (∀ t p, state (name,c) (raw+delta p) t - state (name,c) raw t = path t p) ∧
        (∀ j, test j ≠ 0 → state (name,c) raw (Fin.last r) j = target j))).card
    let pairing := fun (b c : S) => ∑ t : Fin r, dotProduct (b t) (c t)
    let countBits := (r+1)*k
    let w := Nat.log2 countBits + 1
    let common := (3+s+(r+1)*s)*k
    let inputs := common + r*k
    ∃ (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit) (nz neg : Fin (inputs+C.size))
      (expo : Fin w → Fin (inputs+C.size)),
      PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C ∧ PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack inputs C ∧
      C.output = nz.val ∧
      C.size ≤ 65536*(r+1)*((k+1)*(k+s+1)+(w+1)^2) ∧
      ∀ (raw : W) (delta : Fin s → W) (path : Fin (r+1) → Fin s → W) (test target : W) (b : S),
        let xs := encodeInput raw delta path test target ++ coords b
        let coef : ℤ := ∑ c : S, (hits raw delta path test target c : ℤ) *
          (if pairing b c = 0 then (1 : ℤ) else -1)
        let e := Nat.log2 coef.natAbs
        (coef ≠ 0 → coef.natAbs = 2^e) ∧
        (C.wires xs).getD nz.val false = decide (coef ≠ 0) ∧
        (C.wires xs).getD neg.val false = decide (coef < 0) ∧
        (∀ j : Fin w, (C.wires xs).getD (expo j).val false = e.testBit j.val)
changed.unlocks: Prices one exact spectrum coefficient using ordinary gates, allowing computation of schedule counts from observed parities.
changed.context: Each tested difference is a constraint on two adjacent mixed bits. Mask the four entries of an ordinary signed two-state transfer and take its cyclic trace for each input-mask lift through the mixer. Physical spacings give at most sixteen lifts, obtained by a fixed linear section and kernel offsets. Use signed adders for the traces. On a nonempty affine fiber the phase is quadratic, so each nonzero local sum has power-of-two magnitude. Combine signs, exponents, initial compatibility and the terminal factor. Estimate 270 minutes.

changed.title: Counting cyclic keys by affine prefixes and the rank of the final quadratic tests
changed.statement:
∀ (k m r t p h : Nat) (hk : 0 < k),
  let F := ZMod 2
  let W := Fin k → F
  let E := Fin m → F
  let ix := fun n : Nat => (⟨n % k, Nat.mod_lt _ hk⟩ : Fin k)
  let rot := fun (s : Nat) (x : W) (j : Fin k) => x (ix (j.val+k-s % k))
  let gap := fun (b : Bool) => if b then 2 else 1
  let start := fun (b : Bool) => if b then 3 else 1
  let feed := fun (b : Bool) (t : Nat) => if b then 3*(t+1)+1 else 2*t
  let closed := fun (N : Nat) (watch : Bool → Nat → Fin k → Bool) =>
    ∀ (b : Bool) (t : Nat), t < N → ∀ j : Fin k, watch b (t+1) j = true →
      ∀ e : Fin 3, let i := ix (j.val+e.val)
        watch b t i = true ∧ watch b t (ix (i.val+gap b)) = true ∧
        watch b t (ix (i.val+k-gap b % k)) = true
  ∀ (watch : Bool → Nat → Fin k → Bool) (side : Fin t → Bool) (site : Fin t → Fin k),
    closed (r+1) watch → (∀ i, watch (side i) (r+1) (site i) = true) →
    let inputs := (m+2+2*(r+1))*k+t
    ∃ (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit) (flag : Fin (inputs+C.size))
      (ans : Fin (k+1) → Fin (inputs+C.size)),
      PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C ∧ PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack inputs C ∧
      C.output = flag.val ∧
      C.size ≤ 2^40*(k+m+r+t+4)^14*2^(min k p + min t h) ∧
      ∀ (gen : Fin m → W) (name : Bool → W) (c : Bool → Fin (r+1) → W) (target : Fin t → F),
        let state := fun (b : Bool) (key : W) (n : Nat) =>
          ((List.finRange (r+1)).take n).foldl (fun z tick =>
            let y := fun i : Fin k =>
              z i + z (ix (i.val+gap b)) + z (ix (i.val+k-gap b % k))
            fun j : Fin k => y j + (1+y (ix (j.val+1)))*y (ix (j.val+2)) +
              rot (feed b tick.val) key j + c b tick j) (rot (start b) key + name b)
        let shift := fun a : E => ∑ i : Fin m, a i • gen i
        let probe := fun (key : W) (i : Fin t) => state (side i) key (r+1) (site i)
        let polar := fun (a : W) => (fun (i : Fin t) (jl : Fin m × Fin m) =>
          probe a i + probe (a+gen jl.1) i + probe (a+gen jl.2) i +
            probe (a+gen jl.1+gen jl.2) i : Matrix (Fin t) (Fin m × Fin m) F)
        let good := k - Module.finrank F (Submodule.span F (Set.range gen)) ≤ p ∧
          (∀ (a : W) (b : Bool) (n : Nat), n ≤ r → ∀ j : Fin k, watch b n j = true →
            ∀ x y : E, state b a n j + state b (a+shift x) n j + state b (a+shift y) n j +
              state b (a+shift x+shift y) n j = 0) ∧
          (∀ a : W, Matrix.rank (polar a) ≤ h)
        let pack := fun w : W => List.ofFn (fun j : Fin k => decide (w j ≠ 0))
        let bits := (List.ofFn (fun i => pack (gen i))).flatten ++ pack (name false) ++
          pack (name true) ++ (List.ofFn (fun i => pack (c false i))).flatten ++
          (List.ofFn (fun i => pack (c true i))).flatten ++
          List.ofFn (fun i : Fin t => decide (target i ≠ 0))
        let wire := fun i : Fin (inputs+C.size) => (C.wires bits).getD i.val false
        let count := ((Finset.univ : Finset W).filter (fun key => ∀ i, probe key i = target i)).card
        (wire flag = true ↔ good) ∧
          (∀ i : Fin (k+1), wire (ans i) = ((if wire flag then count else 0).testBit i.val))

changed.context: Reduce the directions to a basis, extend to all raw keys, and enumerate the quotient up to the codimension cap. In each coset use generator pairs to check the prefix. Add distinct coset totals and mask on failure. Estimated 260 minutes.

changed.title: A fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT circuit counts cyclic words modulo two with size linear in the cap on boundary pairs of odd multiplicity
changed.statement:
∀ (n w K : Nat) (hn : 0 < n), w ≤ n → 2^w ≤ K → K ≤ 4^w →
  let D := 2^w
  let stride := 2^(w+1)
  let L := n-w
  let I := n*stride + 2*D
  let pos := fun (offset : Nat) => (⟨offset % n, Nat.mod_lt _ hn⟩ : Fin n)
  ∃ (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit) (capWire : Fin (L+1) → Fin (I+C.size)),
    PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C ∧
    PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack I C ∧ C.output < I+C.size ∧
    C.size ≤ 1048576*(n+1)*K*(w+1)^3 ∧
    ∀ (table : Fin n → Nat → Bool) (seedMask endMask : Nat → Bool),
      let inputs := (List.range (n*stride)).map (fun a => table (pos (a/stride)) (a % stride)) ++
        (List.range D).map seedMask ++ (List.range D).map endMask
      let oddPairs := fun (h : Nat) =>
        ((List.range (D*D)).filter (fun edge =>
          (((List.range (2^(w+h))).filter (fun bits =>
            bits % D == edge % D && (bits >>> h) % D == edge / D &&
            (List.range h).all (fun site => table (pos site) ((bits >>> site) % stride)))).length.testBit 0))).length
      let good := fun (h : Nat) => ∀ t ≤ h, oddPairs t ≤ K
      let cyclicPattern := fun (word start : Nat) =>
        (List.range (w+1)).foldl (fun (acc j : Nat) =>
          acc ||| ((word.testBit ((start+j) % n)).toNat <<< j)) 0
      let count := ((List.range (2^n)).filter (fun x =>
        seedMask (x % D) && endMask ((x >>> L) % D) &&
        (List.range n).all (fun i => table (pos i) (cyclicPattern x i)))).length
      (∀ j : Fin (L+1), (C.wires inputs).getD (capWire j).val false = true ↔ good j.val) ∧
      (C.eval inputs = true ↔ good L ∧ count.testBit 0 = true)

changed.title: Unsatisfiable circuit encodings exclude one-hot graph representations with input-only or counted NOT gates
changed.statement:
∀ (left right budget : ℕ) (mask : List ℕ),
  let n := left + right
  let s := budget
  let wd : ℕ := 2 ^ n + n + s + 2
  let ix (kd j a : ℕ) : ℕ := (kd * (s + 1) + j) * wd + a
  let P (v : ℕ) : ℕ := 2 * v + 2
  let Q (v : ℕ) : ℕ := 2 * v + 3
  let L (v : ℕ) (b : Bool) : ℕ := if b then P v else Q v
  let fOp : List (List ℕ) :=
    (List.range s).map fun j => [P (ix 0 j 0), P (ix 0 j 1), P (ix 0 j 2),
      P (ix 0 j 3)]
  let fSrcAlo : List (List ℕ) :=
    [1, 2].flatMap fun e => (List.range s).map fun j =>
      (List.range (n + j + 1)).map fun k => P (ix e j k)
  let srcEq (e j k r : ℕ) : List (List ℕ) :=
    if k < n then [[Q (ix e j k), L (ix (e + 3) j r) (r.testBit k)]]
    else if k < n + j then
      [[Q (ix e j k), Q (ix (e + 3) j r), P (ix 3 (k - n) r)],
       [Q (ix e j k), P (ix (e + 3) j r), Q (ix 3 (k - n) r)]]
    else [[Q (ix e j k), Q (ix (e + 3) j r)]]
  let fSrcEq (rows : List ℕ) : List (List ℕ) :=
    [1, 2].flatMap fun e => (List.range s).flatMap fun j => rows.flatMap fun r =>
      (List.range (n + j + 1)).flatMap fun k => srcEq e j k r
  let gateCl (j r : ℕ) : List (List ℕ) :=
    [[Q (ix 0 j 0), Q (ix 3 j r), P (ix 4 j r)],
     [Q (ix 0 j 0), Q (ix 3 j r), P (ix 5 j r)],
     [Q (ix 0 j 0), P (ix 3 j r), Q (ix 4 j r), Q (ix 5 j r)],
     [Q (ix 0 j 1), P (ix 3 j r), Q (ix 4 j r)],
     [Q (ix 0 j 1), P (ix 3 j r), Q (ix 5 j r)],
     [Q (ix 0 j 1), Q (ix 3 j r), P (ix 4 j r), P (ix 5 j r)],
     [Q (ix 0 j 2), P (ix 3 j r)],
     [Q (ix 0 j 3), P (ix 3 j r), P (ix 4 j r)],
     [Q (ix 0 j 3), Q (ix 3 j r), Q (ix 4 j r)]]
  let fGate (rows : List ℕ) : List (List ℕ) :=
    (List.range s).flatMap fun j => rows.flatMap fun r => gateCl j r
  let fOutAlo : List (List ℕ) := [(List.range (n + s + 1)).map fun k => P (ix 6 0 k)]
  let outEq (g : ℕ → Bool) (k r : ℕ) : List (List ℕ) :=
    if k < n then (if r.testBit k = g r then [] else [[Q (ix 6 0 k)]])
    else if k < n + s then [[Q (ix 6 0 k), L (ix 3 (k - n) r) (g r)]]
    else if g r = true then [[Q (ix 6 0 k)]] else []
  let fOutEq (g : ℕ → Bool) (rows : List ℕ) : List (List ℕ) :=
    rows.flatMap fun r => (List.range (n + s + 1)).flatMap fun k => outEq g k r
  let fOut : List (List ℕ) :=
    if s = 0 then [] else [[P (ix 6 0 (n + s - 1)), P (ix 7 (s - 1) 0)]]
  let fPad : List (List ℕ) :=
    (List.range s).flatMap fun j =>
      [[Q (ix 7 j 0), P (ix 0 j 2)], [Q (ix 7 j 0), P (ix 1 j (n + j))],
       [Q (ix 7 j 0), P (ix 2 j (n + j))], [P (ix 7 j 0), Q (ix 0 j 2)],
       [P (ix 7 j 0), Q (ix 1 j (n + j))], [P (ix 7 j 0), Q (ix 2 j (n + j))]]
  let fPre : List (List ℕ) :=
    (List.range (s - 1)).map fun j => [Q (ix 7 (j + 1) 0), P (ix 7 j 0)]
  let fPadRd : List (List ℕ) :=
    (List.range s).flatMap fun j => (List.range j).flatMap fun i =>
      [[Q (ix 7 i 0), Q (ix 1 j (n + i))], [Q (ix 7 i 0), Q (ix 2 j (n + i))]]
  let fNot : List (List ℕ) :=
    (List.range s).flatMap fun j => (List.range (n + j + 1)).map fun k =>
      [Q (ix 0 j 3), Q (ix 1 j k), P (ix 2 j k)]
  let fNotNot : List (List ℕ) :=
    (List.range s).flatMap fun j => (List.range j).map fun i =>
      [Q (ix 0 j 3), Q (ix 0 i 3), Q (ix 1 j (n + i))]
  let fOrd : List (List ℕ) :=
    (List.range s).flatMap fun j => (List.range (n + j + 1)).flatMap fun k =>
      (List.range (k + 1)).map fun l =>
        [Q (ix 1 j k), Q (ix 2 j l), P (ix 7 j 0)] ++
          if l = k then [P (ix 0 j 3)] else []
  let fUsed : List (List ℕ) :=
    (List.range (s - 1)).map fun j =>
      ((List.range (s - 1 - j)).map fun t => P (ix 1 (j + 1 + t) (n + j))) ++
      ((List.range (s - 1 - j)).map fun t => P (ix 2 (j + 1 + t) (n + j))) ++
        [P (ix 7 j 0)]
  let enc (g : ℕ → Bool) (rows : List ℕ) : List (List ℕ) :=
    fOp ++ fSrcAlo ++ fSrcEq rows ++ fGate rows ++ fOutAlo ++
      fOutEq g rows ++ fOut ++ fPad ++ fPre ++ fPadRd ++ fOrd ++
      fUsed ++ fNot ++ fNotNot
  let lexBase (j : ℕ) : List ℕ :=
    [P (ix 7 j 0), P (ix 1 (j + 1) (n + j)), P (ix 2 (j + 1) (n + j))]
  let fLex : List (List ℕ) :=
    (List.range (s - 1)).flatMap fun j =>
      (List.range (n + j + 1)).flatMap fun a =>
        ((List.range a).map fun b => [Q (ix 1 j a), Q (ix 1 (j + 1) b)] ++ lexBase j) ++
        (List.range (n + j + 1)).flatMap fun c =>
          ((List.range c).map fun d =>
            [Q (ix 1 j a), Q (ix 1 (j + 1) a), Q (ix 2 j c), Q (ix 2 (j + 1) d)] ++
              lexBase j) ++
          [[Q (ix 1 j a), Q (ix 1 (j + 1) a), Q (ix 2 j c), Q (ix 2 (j + 1) c),
              Q (ix 0 j 1)] ++ lexBase j,
           [Q (ix 1 j a), Q (ix 1 (j + 1) a), Q (ix 2 j c), Q (ix 2 (j + 1) c),
              Q (ix 0 (j + 1) 0)] ++ lexBase j]
  let enc2 (g : ℕ → Bool) (rows : List ℕ) : List (List ℕ) := enc g rows ++ fLex
  let rows := (List.range left).flatMap fun i =>
    (List.range right).map fun j => 2^i + 2^(left+j)
  let value := fun (r : ℕ) => (mask.getD (Nat.log2 (r % 2^left)) 0).testBit (Nat.log2 (r / 2^left))
  let base := enc2 value rows
  let rawOnly := (List.range s).flatMap fun j =>
    (List.range (j+1)).map fun k => [Q (ix 0 j 3), Q (ix 1 j (n+k))]
  let capped := fun (bound : ℕ) =>
    (List.sublistsLen (bound+1) (List.range s)).map fun js => js.map fun j => Q (ix 0 j 3)
  let graph := fun (u : Fin left) (v : Fin right) => (mask.getD u.val 0).testBit v.val
  (¬ PEqualNP.Defs.LratEncoding.FormulaSat (base ++ rawOnly) →
    ¬ ∃ C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit, PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C ∧
      C.size ≤ budget ∧
      (∀ g ∈ C.gates, g.op = PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.not → ∃ i < left + right, g.inputs = [i]) ∧
      PEqualNP.Represents.Represents graph C) ∧
    ∀ j : ℕ, ¬ PEqualNP.Defs.LratEncoding.FormulaSat (base ++ capped j) →
      ¬ ∃ C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit, PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C ∧
        C.size ≤ budget ∧ PEqualNP.NotBracket.notCount C ≤ j ∧
        PEqualNP.Represents.Represents graph C

Its satisfying valuation also meets each forbidden-source clause or each forbidden set of inversion slots. Contradict the assumed unsatisfiability. Allow three to six hours.

changed.title: Two overlapping lists of adjacent products on a binary string require two parity questions per three sites up to a bounded additive error
changed.statement:
∀ h : ℕ, 3 ≤ h →
  let F := ZMod 2
  let admits := fun (n : ℕ) (target : (Fin n → F) → Bool → Fin h → F) (d : ℕ) =>
    let W := Fin n → F
    let D := W →ₗ[F] F
    let run := fun (ask : Fin d → ℕ → D) (x : W) =>
      (List.finRange d).foldl (fun t j => 2*t + (if ask j t x = 0 then 0 else 1)) (0 : ℕ)
    ∃ (ask : Fin d → ℕ → D) (readout : ℕ → Bool → Fin h → D)
      (bias : ℕ → Bool → Fin h → F),
      ∀ x b i, target x b i = readout (run ask x) b i x + bias (run ask x) b i
  let line := fun (y : Fin (h+4) → F) (b : Bool) (i : Fin h) =>
    let a := fun j : ℕ => y (Fin.ofNat (h+4) (i.val+j))
    if b then (a 0 + a 1 + a 2) * (a 1 + a 2 + a 3) else a 3 * a 4
  (∀ d : ℕ, admits (h+4) line d → h-2-(h-1)/3 ≤ d) ∧
    admits (h+4) line (h+4-(h+4)/3)
changed.unlocks: Bounds how many common parity answers are needed for joint affine recovery on a finite one-round output window after projection to independent bits.
changed.context: Restrict to the zero transcript. On h-1 common sites, adjacent forms in each of the two lists must be dependent. Group successive equal nonzero labels across zeros. Distinct labels cannot have two zeros between them. At a one-zero transition an interior singleton gives adjacent sum labels A and A+B, which are independent. Each group and its outgoing gap use at least three sites except the leading group may use two and the final group one. For the upper bound repeat two equal free bits and one zero, fixing any tail. Query the annihilator. Allow 120 to 210 minutes.

changed.title: Translating an affine guard can change the exact adaptive parity depth by a linear number of questions
changed.statement:
∀ (n : Nat), 4 ≤ n →
  let F := ZMod 2
  let V := Fin n → F
  let P := F × V
  ∀ (K : Submodule F V) (center : V) (tilt : V →ₗ[F] F) (offset : F) (q : Nat),
    let copyBit := fun x : V => tilt x + offset +
      (if @decide (x-center ∈ K) (Classical.propDecidable _) then (1 : F) else 0)
    let dim := Module.finrank F K
    let codim := n-dim
    let aligned := n+1 - max 1 (min (n/2) (min codim (dim+1)))
    let cost := if @decide (center ∈ K) (Classical.propDecidable _) then aligned
      else if 2 ≤ codim then n-1 else n
    let success := ∃ (ask : (j : Fin q) → (Fin j.val → F) → (P →ₗ[F] F))
        (ans : P → Fin q → F) (decode : (Fin q → F) → Bool),
      (∀ (p : P) (j : Fin q), ans p j =
        ask j (fun earlier => ans p ⟨earlier.val, Nat.lt_trans earlier.isLt j.isLt⟩) p) ∧
      (∀ b : F, decode (ans (b,0)) = false) ∧
      (∀ x : V, x ≠ 0 → decode (ans (copyBit x,x)) = true)
    Iff success (cost ≤ q)
changed.unlocks: Predicts the query cost of a conjunction of independent affine guards from its codimension and whether it contains the negative anchor.
changed.context: Follow the two rejected transcripts to get disjoint spaces of dimension s=n+1-q requiring opposite affine copies. For a guard through zero, on one space the off-zero support size is 2^j-1, forcing trivial intersection with K. On the other it is an affine hyperplane or the whole space. Choose coordinate spaces to attain the bounds. For a translated guard a hyperplane avoids it, and two disjoint planes can have odd and zero intersections. Full proof in notes/seat-rlift-1/output-labels/guard-and-extra-copies.md.

changed.title: Three binary products on seven shared signals give a matrix of rank at most sixteen
changed.statement:
∀ bits : Fin 8 → ZMod 2,
  let output := fun (z : Fin 7 → ZMod 2) =>
    let p := z 1 * z 2
    let q := (z 3 + bits 0 * p) * (z 4 + bits 1 * p)
    let left := z 5 + bits 2 * p + bits 3 * q
    let right := z 6 + bits 4 * p + bits 5 * q
    z 0 + bits 6 * p + bits 7 * q + left * right
  (Matrix.of (fun x y : Fin 7 → ZMod 2 => output (x + y))).rank ≤ 16
changed.unlocks: A submatrix restriction transfers the finite ceiling to arbitrary row and column label sets in this three-product form.
changed.context: For each of the 256 schedules form the 128 rows as 128-bit words. Keep a basis by eliminating the highest set bit. Record its row indices and elimination coefficients. Check at most sixteen pivots and replay every row as a binary sum of selected rows. Turn the replay into a rectangular matrix factorization, then apply rank_mul_le_left and rank_le_card_width. The complete enumeration is in the three-products research note. Budget 120 to 240 minutes.

changed.title: Exact shared parity-query depth for both complete one-round output words at widths divisible by three
changed.statement:
∀ (k : ℕ) (hk : 0 < k), 3 ∣ k →
  let h := k
  let F := ZMod 2
  let admits := fun (n : ℕ) (target : (Fin n → F) → Bool → Fin h → F) (d : ℕ) =>
    let W := Fin n → F
    let D := W →ₗ[F] F
    let run := fun (ask : Fin d → ℕ → D) (x : W) =>
      (List.finRange d).foldl (fun t j => 2*t + (if ask j t x = 0 then 0 else 1)) (0 : ℕ)
    ∃ (ask : Fin d → ℕ → D) (readout : ℕ → Bool → Fin h → D)
      (bias : ℕ → Bool → Fin h → F),
      ∀ x b i, target x b i = readout (run ask x) b i x + bias (run ask x) b i
  let W := Fin k → F
  let ix := fun j : ℕ => (⟨j % k, Nat.mod_lt _ hk⟩ : Fin k)
  let rot := fun (s : ℕ) (x : W) (i : Fin k) => x (ix (i.val+k-s % k))
  let mix := fun (g : ℕ) (x : W) (i : Fin k) =>
    x i + x (ix (i.val+g)) + x (ix (i.val+k-g % k))
  let step := fun (x : W) (i : Fin k) => x i + (1+x (ix (i.val+1))) * x (ix (i.val+2))
  ∀ (start d : ℕ) (row col c₁ c₂ : W),
    let target := fun (x : W) (b : Bool) (i : Fin h) =>
      let site := ix (start + i.val)
      if b then step (mix 2 (rot 3 x + col)) site + rot 4 x site + c₂ site
      else step (mix 1 (rot 1 x + row)) site + x site + c₁ site
    admits k target d ↔ (if k = 3 then 0 else 2*(k/3)-1) ≤ d
changed.unlocks: Gives the common parity-conditioning cost for both whole outputs when the key mix has a two-dimensional kernel.
changed.context: In mixed coordinates the two adjacent-product tests see labels a and their three-term sums. Each group of equal nonzero labels and its outgoing gap consume at least three sites when there are distinct groups. At m groups all runs therefore have length two with single zero gaps. The three residue parities must agree, forcing the sum of those m run labels to vanish. The mixed dimension is at most m-1 and the two-dimensional mix kernel adds two. Paired runs with even-sum labels attain this bound on every coset. Width three mixes to a constant word. Allow 150 to 270 minutes.

changed.title: Two one-round output windows on the same cyclic key have exactly the parity-query cost of one open binary string
changed.statement:
∀ (h k : ℕ) (hk : 0 < k), h+6 ≤ k →
  let F := ZMod 2
  let admits := fun (n : ℕ) (target : (Fin n → F) → Bool → Fin h → F) (d : ℕ) =>
    let W := Fin n → F
    let D := W →ₗ[F] F
    let run := fun (ask : Fin d → ℕ → D) (x : W) =>
      (List.finRange d).foldl (fun t j => 2*t + (if ask j t x = 0 then 0 else 1)) (0 : ℕ)
    ∃ (ask : Fin d → ℕ → D) (readout : ℕ → Bool → Fin h → D)
      (bias : ℕ → Bool → Fin h → F),
      ∀ x b i, target x b i = readout (run ask x) b i x + bias (run ask x) b i
  let line := fun (y : Fin (h+4) → F) (b : Bool) (i : Fin h) =>
    let a := fun j : ℕ => y (Fin.ofNat (h+4) (i.val+j))
    if b then (a 0 + a 1 + a 2) * (a 1 + a 2 + a 3) else a 3 * a 4
  let W := Fin k → F
  let ix := fun j : ℕ => (⟨j % k, Nat.mod_lt _ hk⟩ : Fin k)
  let rot := fun (s : ℕ) (x : W) (i : Fin k) => x (ix (i.val+k-s % k))
  let mix := fun (g : ℕ) (x : W) (i : Fin k) =>
    x i + x (ix (i.val+g)) + x (ix (i.val+k-g % k))
  let step := fun (x : W) (i : Fin k) => x i + (1+x (ix (i.val+1))) * x (ix (i.val+2))
  ∀ (start d : ℕ) (row col c₁ c₂ : W),
    let target := fun (x : W) (b : Bool) (i : Fin h) =>
      let site := ix (start + i.val)
      if b then step (mix 2 (rot 3 x + col)) site + rot 4 x site + c₂ site
      else step (mix 1 (rot 1 x + row)) site + x site + c₁ site
    admits k target d ↔ admits (h+4) line d

changed.title: Fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT circuits count names and schedules satisfying runtime parity observations at bounded observation rank
changed.statement:
∀ (k r s : Nat) (hk : 0 < k),
  let F := ZMod 2
  let W := Fin k → F
  let ix := fun t : Nat => (⟨t % k, Nat.mod_lt _ hk⟩ : Fin k)
  let rot := fun (amount : Nat) (x : W) (j : Fin k) => x (ix (j.val+k-amount % k))
  let layer := fun (gap : Nat) (x : W) =>
    let m := fun (j : Fin k) => x j + x (ix (j.val+gap)) + x (ix (j.val+k-gap % k))
    fun (j : Fin k) => m j + (1+m (ix (j.val+1))) * m (ix (j.val+2))
  ∀ col : Bool,
    let initial := if col then 3 else 1
    let gap := if col then 2 else 1
    let inject := fun t : Nat => if col then 3*(t+1)+1 else 2*t
    let state := fun (data : W × (Fin r → W)) (key : W) (time : Fin (r+1)) =>
      ((List.finRange r).take time.val).foldl (fun v tick =>
        layer gap v + rot (inject tick.val) key + data.2 tick) (rot initial key + data.1)
    let S := Fin r → W
    let encodeInput := fun (raw : W) (delta : Fin s → W)
      (path : Fin (r+1) → Fin s → W) (test target : W) =>
      let bits := fun (x : W) => (List.finRange k).map (fun j => decide (x j ≠ 0))
      bits raw ++ (List.finRange s).flatMap (fun p => bits (delta p)) ++
      (List.finRange (r+1)).flatMap (fun t =>
        (List.finRange s).flatMap (fun p => bits (path t p))) ++ bits test ++ bits target
    let coords := fun (b : S) => (List.finRange r).flatMap (fun t =>
      (List.finRange k).map (fun j => decide (b t j ≠ 0)))
    let hits := fun (raw : W) (delta : Fin s → W) (path : Fin (r+1) → Fin s → W)
      (test target : W) (c : S) =>
      ((Finset.univ : Finset W).filter (fun name =>
        (∀ t p, state (name,c) (raw+delta p) t - state (name,c) raw t = path t p) ∧
        (∀ j, test j ≠ 0 → state (name,c) raw (Fin.last r) j = target j))).card

    let countBits := (r+1)*k
    let w := Nat.log2 countBits + 1
    let common := (3+s+(r+1)*s)*k
    ∀ q cap : Nat,
      let p := min cap (r*k)
      let inputs := common+q*r*k+q
      let length := countBits+p+3
      ∃ (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit) (overflow : Fin (inputs+C.size))
        (answer : Fin (countBits+1) → Fin (inputs+C.size)),
        PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C ∧ PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack inputs C ∧
        C.output = overflow.val ∧
        C.size ≤ 65536*(q+1)*(r*k+2)^3 +
          2^p * (524288*(r+1)*((k+1)*(k+s+p+1)+(w+1)^2) + 256*length^2) ∧
        ∀ (raw : W) (delta : Fin s → W) (path : Fin (r+1) → Fin s → W)
          (test target : W) (obs : Fin q → S) (wanted : Fin q → F),
          let xs := encodeInput raw delta path test target ++
            (List.finRange q).flatMap (fun j => coords (obs j)) ++
            (List.finRange q).map (fun j => decide (wanted j ≠ 0))

changed.title: Four boundary bits determine the exact parity-query cost for products in overlapping five-bit windows
changed.statement:
∀ (h t : ℕ) (a b : Fin h → Fin t → Fin 32) (d : ℕ),
  let F := ZMod 2
  let W := Fin (h+4) → F
  let D := W →ₗ[F] F
  let operand := fun (x : W) (i : Fin h) (mask : Fin 32) =>
    ∑ j : Fin 5, if mask.val.testBit j.val then x (Fin.ofNat (h+4) (i.val+j.val)) else 0
  let run := fun (ask : Fin d → ℕ → D) (x : W) =>
    (List.finRange d).foldl (fun tr j => 2*tr + (if ask j tr x = 0 then 0 else 1)) (0 : ℕ)
  let advance := fun (st : ℕ × Finset ℕ) (atSite : Fin t → ℕ) =>
    let extended := (List.finRange t).foldl (fun (s : Finset ℕ) j =>
      s ∪ s.image (fun v => v ^^^ atSite j)) st.2
    let even := extended.filter (fun v => v % 2 = 0)
    (st.1 + (if even = extended then 0 else 1), even.image (fun v => v / 2))
  let selectMask := fun (u v : Fin 32) (c : Fin 3) =>
    if c.val = 0 then u.val else if c.val = 1 then v.val else u.val ^^^ v.val
  (∃ (ask : Fin d → ℕ → D) (readout : ℕ → Fin h → Fin t → D)
      (bias : ℕ → Fin h → Fin t → F),
    ∀ x i j, operand x i (a i j) * operand x i (b i j) =
      readout (run ask x) i j x + bias (run ask x) i j) ↔
  ∃ pick : Fin h → Fin t → Fin 3,
    let last := (List.finRange h).foldl (fun st i =>
      advance st (fun j => selectMask (a i j) (b i j) (pick i j))) ((0, {0}) : ℕ × Finset ℕ)
    last.1 + Nat.log2 last.2.card ≤ d
changed.unlocks: Provides the exact cost at arbitrary lengths and independent site masks for the two one-round output windows after their reduction to independent bits.
changed.context: For each product choose its left mask, right mask or their XOR. The least joint rank of chosen forms is the adaptive query depth. Sweep from left to right. Keep the span of combinations vanishing on all forgotten sites. Close it under adding the chosen five-bit masks. Dropping the current coordinate costs one rank exactly when an odd mask is present. Shift the even masks to obtain the next boundary space. Charge its dimension at the end. All later masks vanish on every forgotten site. Allow 120 to 240 minutes.

changed.title: For repeated five-bit product masks the minimum boundary cost eventually gains a fixed amount over each period
changed.statement:
∀ (t : ℕ) (a b : Fin t → Fin 32),
  let advance := fun (st : ℕ × Finset ℕ) (atSite : Fin t → ℕ) =>
    let extended := (List.finRange t).foldl (fun (s : Finset ℕ) j =>
      s ∪ s.image (fun v => v ^^^ atSite j)) st.2
    let even := extended.filter (fun v => v % 2 = 0)
    (st.1 + (if even = extended then 0 else 1), even.image (fun v => v / 2))
  let selectMask := fun (u v : Fin 32) (c : Fin 3) =>
    if c.val = 0 then u.val else if c.val = 1 then v.val else u.val ^^^ v.val
  let cost := fun (h : ℕ) (pick : Fin h → Fin t → Fin 3) =>
    let last := (List.finRange h).foldl (fun st i =>
      advance st (fun j => selectMask (a j) (b j) (pick i j))) ((0, {0}) : ℕ × Finset ℕ)
    last.1 + Nat.log2 last.2.card
  let minimum := fun (h d : ℕ) =>
    (∃ p : Fin h → Fin t → Fin 3, cost h p = d) ∧
    ∀ p : Fin h → Fin t → Fin 3, d ≤ cost h p
  ∃ H q r : ℕ, 0 < q ∧
    (∀ h d : ℕ, H ≤ h → minimum h d → minimum (h+q) (d+r)) ∧
    ((∃ B : ℕ, ∀ h d : ℕ, minimum h d → 2*h ≤ 3*d+B ∧ 3*d ≤ 2*h+B) →
      3*r = 2*q)

changed.context: Start the recurrence from each four-bit subspace S. For fixed choices the cost is the rank after adjoining S to the selected masks. Relative to starting at zero this adds between zero and four, even after minimizing. Subtract the zero-start minimum from every entry of this finite vector. The one-site minimum update commutes with addition of constants, so equal normalized vectors have equal successors. Two lengths must repeat. Iterate the resulting drift and use the bounded discrepancy to get 3r = 2q. Allow 120 to 240 minutes.

changed.title: Sharp number of extra witness copies needed for a bounded-degree default bit to permit a specified adaptive parity depth
changed.statement:
∀ (n q d budget : Nat), 0 < q → q < n → 0 < d →
  let F := ZMod 2
  let V := Fin n → F
  let P := F × V
  let dim := n+1-q
  let success := fun (poly : MvPolynomial (Fin n) F) (extra : Finset V) =>
    ∃ (ask : (j : Fin q) → (Fin j.val → F) → (P →ₗ[F] F))
        (ans : P → Fin q → F) (decode : (Fin q → F) → Bool),
      (∀ (p : P) (j : Fin q), ans p j =
        ask j (fun earlier => ans p ⟨earlier.val, Nat.lt_trans earlier.isLt j.isLt⟩) p) ∧
      (∀ b : F, decode (ans (b,0)) = false) ∧
      (∀ x : V, x ≠ 0 → ∃ b : F,
        (b = MvPolynomial.eval x poly ∨ x ∈ extra) ∧ decode (ans (b,x)) = true)
  Iff
    (∃ (poly : MvPolynomial (Fin n) F) (extra : Finset V),
      poly.totalDegree ≤ d ∧ (0 : V) ∉ extra ∧ extra.card ≤ budget ∧ success poly extra)
    (2*dim ≤ n ∧ 2^(dim-d) ≤ budget+1)

changed.title: Exact least-squares error and minimum fixed schedule parity count for predicting shared-key history multiplicities
changed.statement:
∀ (k r s : Nat) (hk : 0 < k),
  let F := ZMod 2
  let W := Fin k → F
  let ix := fun t : Nat => (⟨t % k, Nat.mod_lt _ hk⟩ : Fin k)
  let rot := fun (amount : Nat) (x : W) (j : Fin k) => x (ix (j.val+k-amount % k))
  let layer := fun (gap : Nat) (x : W) =>
    let m := fun (j : Fin k) => x j + x (ix (j.val+gap)) + x (ix (j.val+k-gap % k))
    fun (j : Fin k) => m j + (1+m (ix (j.val+1))) * m (ix (j.val+2))
  ∀ (col : Bool) (raw : W) (delta : Fin s → W)
    (path : Fin (r+1) → Fin s → W) (test : Finset (Fin k)) (target : W),
    let initial := if col then 3 else 1
    let gap := if col then 2 else 1
    let inject := fun t : Nat => if col then 3*(t+1)+1 else 2*t
    let state := fun (data : W × (Fin r → W)) (key : W) (time : Fin (r+1)) =>
      ((List.finRange r).take time.val).foldl (fun v tick =>
        layer gap v + rot (inject tick.val) key + data.2 tick) (rot initial key + data.1)
    let S := Fin r → W
    let valid := ∀ p, path 0 p = rot initial (delta p)
    let localSet := fun (t : Fin r) => (Finset.univ : Finset W).filter (fun v => ∀ p : Fin s,
      layer gap (v+path t.castSucc p) - layer gap v + rot (inject t.val) (delta p) = path t.succ p)
    let hits := fun (c : S) => ((Finset.univ : Finset W).filter (fun name =>
      (∀ t p, state (name,c) (raw+delta p) t - state (name,c) raw t = path t p) ∧
      (∀ j ∈ test, state (name,c) raw (Fin.last r) j = target j))).card
    let prev := fun (b : S) (j : Nat) => ∑ t : Fin r, (if t.val+1 = j then b t else 0)
    let pairing := fun (b c : S) => ∑ t : Fin r, dotProduct (b t) (c t)
    let phase := fun (b : S) (t : Fin r) (v : W) => dotProduct (prev b t.val) v +
      dotProduct (b t) (layer gap v + rot (inject t.val) raw)
    let polar := fun (u v : W) => layer gap (u+v) - layer gap u - layer gap v + layer gap 0
    let dirs := fun (t : Fin r) => (Finset.univ : Finset W).filter
      (fun z => ∀ p, polar z (path t.castSucc p) = 0)
    let rad := fun (b : S) (t : Fin r) => (dirs t).filter
      (fun z => ∀ u ∈ dirs t, dotProduct (b t) (polar z u) = 0)
    let weight := fun (b : S) (t : Fin r) =>
      if ∃ v ∈ localSet t, ∀ z ∈ rad b t, phase b t (v+z) = phase b t v
      then (dirs t).card * (rad b t).card else 0
    let energy := fun b : S =>
      if valid ∧ (∀ j : Fin k, j ∉ test → prev b r j = 0) then
        (2 : Nat)^(2*(k-test.card)) * (∏ t : Fin r, weight b t)
      else 0
    let supp := (Finset.univ : Finset S).filter (fun b => 0 < energy b)
    ∀ q : Nat,
      (∀ Q : S →ₗ[F] (Fin q → F),
        let visible := fun b : S => ∀ z : S, Q z = 0 → pairing b z = 0
        let lost : ℚ := ∑ b ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset S).filter (fun m => ¬visible m), (energy b : ℚ)
        let err := fun (dec : (Fin q → F) → ℚ) =>
          (2 : ℚ)^(k*r) * (∑ z : S, ((hits z : ℚ) - dec (Q z))^2)
        (∀ dec, lost ≤ err dec) ∧ (∃ dec, err dec = lost)) ∧
      ((∃ (Q : S →ₗ[F] (Fin q → F)) (dec : (Fin q → F) → Nat), ∀ z, dec (Q z) = hits z) ↔
        Module.finrank F (Submodule.span F (supp : Set S)) ≤ q)
changed.unlocks: Determines which parities of the schedule preserve the history count and quantifies the loss from discarding the others.
changed.context: For a feasible local difference step the baselines form a translate of the polar kernel of all incoming changes. Square the signed phase sum by shifts in this kernel. Only its radical contributes, with cancellation unless the phase is constant on those shifts. Multiply the round energies and terminal factor. The best decoder is the mean on each query fiber. Character orthogonality discards exactly the masks nontrivial on the query kernel. A basis of the remaining spectral support span realizes exact recovery. Estimate 210 minutes.

changed.title: Generator pairs detect the onset of nonlinearity in a cyclic key history at any depth
changed.statement:
∀ (k m r : Nat) (hk : 0 < k),
  let F := ZMod 2
  let W := Fin k → F
  let E := Fin m → F
  let ix := fun n : Nat => (⟨n % k, Nat.mod_lt _ hk⟩ : Fin k)
  let rot := fun (s : Nat) (x : W) (j : Fin k) => x (ix (j.val+k-s % k))
  let gap := fun (b : Bool) => if b then 2 else 1
  let start := fun (b : Bool) => if b then 3 else 1
  let feed := fun (b : Bool) (t : Nat) => if b then 3*(t+1)+1 else 2*t
  let unit := fun (i j : Fin m) => (if i = j then 1 else 0 : F)
  let closed := fun (N : Nat) (watch : Bool → Nat → Fin k → Bool) =>
    ∀ (b : Bool) (t : Nat), t < N → ∀ j : Fin k, watch b (t+1) j = true →
      ∀ e : Fin 3, let i := ix (j.val+e.val)
        watch b t i = true ∧ watch b t (ix (i.val+gap b)) = true ∧
        watch b t (ix (i.val+k-gap b % k)) = true
  ∀ (watch : Bool → Nat → Fin k → Bool), closed r watch →
  ∀ (base : W) (gen : Fin m → W) (name : Bool → W) (c : Bool → Fin r → W),
    let state := fun (b : Bool) (key : W) (n : Nat) =>
      ((List.finRange r).take n).foldl (fun z tick =>
        let y := fun i : Fin k =>
          z i + z (ix (i.val+gap b)) + z (ix (i.val+k-gap b % k))
        fun j : Fin k => y j + (1+y (ix (j.val+1)))*y (ix (j.val+2)) +
          rot (feed b tick.val) key j + c b tick j) (rot (start b) key + name b)
    let shift := fun a : E => ∑ i : Fin m, a i • gen i
    let atKey := fun (b : Bool) (t : Nat) (j : Fin k) (a : E) => state b (base+shift a) t j
    let defect := fun (b : Bool) (t : Nat) (j : Fin k) (z x y : E) =>
      atKey b t j z + atKey b t j (z+x) + atKey b t j (z+y) + atKey b t j (z+x+y)
    let affineThrough := fun h : Nat => ∀ (b : Bool) (t : Nat), t ≤ h → ∀ j : Fin k,
      watch b t j = true → ∀ x y : E, defect b t j 0 x y = 0
    (∀ h : Nat, h ≤ r → (affineThrough h ↔ ∀ (b : Bool) (t : Nat), t ≤ h → ∀ j : Fin k,
      watch b t j = true → ∀ i l : Fin m, defect b t j 0 (unit i) (unit l) = 0)) ∧
    (∀ t : Nat, t < r → affineThrough t → ¬affineThrough (t+1) →
      ∃ (b : Bool) (j : Fin k) (i l : Fin m), watch b (t+1) j = true ∧ i ≠ l ∧
        ∀ z : E, defect b (t+1) j z (unit i) (unit l) ≠ 0 ∧
          8 * ((Finset.univ : Finset (E × E)).filter
            (fun xy => defect b (t+1) j z xy.1 xy.2 ≠ 0)).card = 3 * 2^(2*m))
changed.unlocks: Checks the exact affine prefixes used to count entire groups of raw keys in the joint terminal test.
changed.context: Induct on the prefix. At time zero every bit is affine. A watched output at the earliest possible failure is an affine bit plus the product of two affine bits because all predecessor sites are watched. Its polar is A(x)B(y)+A(y)B(x). Its entries on generator pairs determine it. If nonzero one entry witnesses failure at every anchor. The map to the two operand slopes is onto F2 squared, where six of sixteen ordered pairs have determinant one. Allow repeated generators. Estimated 110 minutes.

changed.title: Signed counts on joint cyclic difference fibers from paths and cycles of free components
changed.unlocks: Evaluates squared local factors of a schedule spectrum by counting path and cycle components.
changed.context: Parameterize the fiber by independent flips of free components. Each is a cyclic interval. Contracting intervals, deleting pinned sites and cancelling repeated edges leaves paths and cycles. The polar matrix of the restricted phase is their adjacency matrix. On a path a null vector alternates with a forced endpoint neighbor zero. On a cycle it repeats with period two. Odd components contribute one null bit and even cycles two. Apply the binary quadratic radical formula on the flip coordinates. Estimate 140 minutes.

changed.title: The first two positive error counts for one-hot Sylvester prediction at the exact nonlinear gate budget
changed.statement:
let nonlinear := fun (g : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Gate) =>
  (g.inputs.length == 2) &&
  xor (xor (g.op.eval [false,false]) (g.op.eval [false,true]))
      (xor (g.op.eval [true,false]) (g.op.eval [true,true]))
∀ s : ℕ, 2 ≤ s →
  let N := 4^s
  let V := Fin (2*s) → ZMod 2
  ∀ H : Fin N → Fin N → Bool,
  (∀ a b : Fin N, a ≠ b →
    2 * ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin N)).filter (fun v => H a v ≠ H b v)).card = N) →
  let sylvester := ∃ (row col : Fin N ≃ V) (Q R : Fin N → Bool),
    ∀ i j, H i j = xor (xor (Q i) (R j))
      (decide ((∑ b : Fin (2*s), row i b * col j b) = 1))
  let clone := fun (A B : Fin N → Fin N → Bool) =>
    ∃ i j : Fin N, i ≠ j ∧ ∃ flip : Bool, ∀ x y,
      B x y = if x = i then xor flip (A j y) else A x y
  let valid := fun (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit) =>
    (∀ g ∈ C.gates, g.inputs.length ≤ 2) ∧
    PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack (N+N) C ∧ C.gates.countP nonlinear ≤ s
  let value := fun (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit) (x y : Fin N) =>
    C.eval (PEqualNP.Represents.oneEach x y)
  let errors := fun (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit) =>
    ∑ i : Fin N, ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin N)).filter (fun j => H i j ≠ value C i j)).card
  (∀ C, valid C → errors C + 2 < N →
    sylvester ∧ (errors C = 0 ∨
      (2 * errors C = N ∧ (clone H (value C) ∨ clone (Function.swap H) (Function.swap (value C)))))) ∧
  (sylvester → (∃ C, valid C ∧ 2 * errors C = N) ∧ (∃ C, valid C ∧ errors C + 2 = N))
changed.unlocks: The classification of near-optimal one-hot Hadamard predictions.
changed.context: The Frobenius rank loss is at most 4e/N. Below N errors this forces t=s and rank greater than 5N/8. The triangular spectrum cutoff then makes the predictor a signed sample of Sylvester. Apply the signed sampling gap. One-hot affine lookups realize arbitrary relabellings and signs for the s-gate paired inner-product construction.
