changed.title: Exact minimum support for averaging every cyclic translate of an integer score list of length a power of two
changed.statement:
∀ (a : ℕ) (v : Fin (2^a) → ℕ),
  let I := Fin (2^a)
  let side := fun (j h : ℕ) => (Finset.univ : Finset I).filter (fun i => i.val % (2^(j+1)) = h)
  let active := (Finset.range a).filter (fun j => (List.range (2^j)).any (fun h => decide (
    (∑ i ∈ side j h, v i) ≠ ∑ i ∈ side j (h+2^j), v i)))
  let q := 2^active.card
  let coins := (Finset.univ : Finset I).filter (fun s =>
    (List.range a).all (fun j => !(s.val.testBit j) || decide (j ∈ active)))
  let balanced := fun (p : I → ℝ) =>
    ∀ i i' : I, (∑ s : I, p s * (v (i+s) : ℝ)) = ∑ s : I, p s * (v (i'+s) : ℝ)
  coins.card = q ∧ balanced (fun s => if s ∈ coins then 1/(q : ℝ) else 0) ∧
    ∀ p : I → ℝ, (∀ s, 0 ≤ p s) → (∑ s, p s) = 1 →
      (balanced p ↔ ∀ j ∈ active, ∀ h ∈ Finset.range (2^j),
        (∑ s ∈ side j h, p s) = ∑ s ∈ side j (h+2^j), p s) ∧
      (balanced p → q ≤ ((Finset.univ : Finset I).filter (fun s => 0 < p s)).card)
changed.unlocks: Determines which fair coin positions must split for a cyclic circuit loss profile and supplies a distribution of minimum support.
changed.context: Encode scores and weights as cyclic polynomials, reversing the scores for correlation. At level j, reduction modulo X^(2^j)+1 subtracts the two child sums. A nonzero rational score remainder is invertible there over the rationals by cyclotomic irreducibility, hence also over the reals. The product is constant across indices exactly when all nontrivial factors divide it. At every active level each positive parent mass splits into two positive children. Choosing just the active bits uniformly gives both this support size and the sibling equalities.

changed.title: The density of selector edits inside squares bounds the gate deficit for arbitrary one-hot circuits
changed.statement:
∀ k a : ℕ, (0 < a ∧ 2^a ≤ k) →
  let N := 2^k
  let r := 2^a
  let I := Fin N
  ∀ (T : I → I → Bool) (f g : I → Bool) (A B : Finset I) (q u v : ℕ),
    let F := fun x y : I => xor (x.val.testBit (y.val % r)) (xor (f x) (g y))
    0 < v →
    (∀ i j : I, i ≠ j →
      17+2*(v-1) ≤ (Finset.univ.filter (fun z : I => T i z ≠ T j z)).card ∧
      17+2*(v-1) ≤ (Finset.univ.filter (fun z : I => T z i ≠ T z j)).card) →
    (∀ X Y : Finset I, Disjoint X A → Disjoint Y B → X.card = Y.card →
      ((X ×ˢ Y).filter (fun z => T z.1 z.2 ≠ F z.1 z.2)).card ≤ q*X.card+u) →
    ∀ C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit, (∀ gate ∈ C.gates, gate.inputs.length ≤ 2) →
      let e := (Finset.univ.filter (fun z : I × I =>
        C.eval (PEqualNP.Represents.oneEach z.1 z.2) ≠ T z.1 z.2)).card
      let b := C.gates.countP (fun gate => gate.inputs.length == 2)
      (32*N-(15*b+54+44*(e/v)+A.card+B.card+4*q+2*a*(N/r)))^2 ≤ 4*(e+u)

changed.statement:
∀ k a : ℕ, (6 ≤ a ∧ 2*2^a ≤ k) →
  let N := 2^k

  let I := Fin N

changed.title: Overlaps of XOR shifts characterize switched selector distance and force a two-shift loss beyond the address count
changed.statement:
∀ k a : ℕ, (0 < a ∧ 2^a ≤ k) →
  let N := 2^k
  let r := 2^a
  let I := Fin N
  let target := fun (D : Finset ℕ) (x y : I) =>
    xor (x.val.testBit (y.val % r)) (decide (Nat.xor x.val y.val ∈ D))
  let separated := fun (D : Finset ℕ) (d : ℕ) =>
    ∀ f g : I → Bool,
      let T := fun x y : I => xor (target D x y) (xor (f x) (g y))
      ∀ i j : I, i ≠ j →
        d ≤ (Finset.univ.filter (fun z : I => T i z ≠ T j z)).card ∧
        d ≤ (Finset.univ.filter (fun z : I => T z i ≠ T z j)).card
  ∀ D : Finset ℕ, D ⊆ Finset.range N → 4*D.card ≤ N/r →
    (∀ s : ℕ, separated D (2*s) ↔
      ∀ h : ℕ, 0 < h → h < N → (h % r = 0 ∨ h % (2^r) = 2^r-1) →
        (D.filter (fun z => Nat.xor z h ∈ D)).card + s ≤ D.card) ∧
    ∃ i j : I, i ≠ j ∧ i.val % r = j.val % r ∧
      (Finset.univ.filter (fun x : I => target D x i ≠ target D x j)).card ≤
        2*(if D.card ≤ r then D.card else D.card-2)

changed.title: One nested sequence of XOR shifts attains the selector distance bound at every prefix with quadratic binary-address cost
changed.statement:
∀ k a : ℕ, (2 ≤ a ∧ 2*2^a ≤ k) →
  let N := 2^k
  let r := 2^a
  let I := Fin N
  let target := fun (D : Finset ℕ) (x y : I) =>
    xor (x.val.testBit (y.val % r)) (decide (Nat.xor x.val y.val ∈ D))
  let separated := fun (D : Finset ℕ) (d : ℕ) =>
    ∀ f g : I → Bool,
      let T := fun x y : I => xor (target D x y) (xor (f x) (g y))
      ∀ i j : I, i ≠ j →
        d ≤ (Finset.univ.filter (fun z : I => T i z ≠ T j z)).card ∧
        d ≤ (Finset.univ.filter (fun z : I => T z i ≠ T z j)).card
  let Q := 2^(k/2)
  ∃ enc : Fin Q ↪ I,
    (∀ i : Fin Q, (enc i).val % Q = i.val) ∧
    ∀ t : ℕ, t ≤ Q →
      let D := ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin Q)).filter (fun i => i.val < t)).image (fun i => (enc i).val)
      D.card = t ∧
      PEqualNP.Represents.HasLitSize (k+k) (PEqualNP.Represents.adjFun (k := k) (l := k) (target D))
        (150*(k+1)^2) ∧ separated D (2*(if t ≤ r then t else t-2))

changed.title: Above half the shift support a random choice of small circuits has strictly larger worst-case selector error than an unrestricted table
changed.statement:
∀ k a : ℕ, (6 ≤ a ∧ 2*2^a ≤ k) →
  let N := 2^k
  let r := 2^a
  let I := Fin N
  let target := fun (D : Finset ℕ) (x y : I) =>
    xor (x.val.testBit (y.val % r)) (decide (Nat.xor x.val y.val ∈ D))
  let Q := 2^(k/2)
  let fits := fun C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit =>
    (∀ g ∈ C.gates, g.inputs.length ≤ 2) ∧ 16*(C.gates.countP (fun g => g.inputs.length == 2)) ≤ 33*N
  let table := fun (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit) (x y : I) =>
    C.eval (PEqualNP.Represents.oneEach x y)
  ∃ Γ : Finset ℕ, Γ ⊆ Finset.range N ∧ Γ.card = Q ∧
    PEqualNP.Represents.HasLitSize (k+k) (PEqualNP.Represents.adjFun (k := k) (l := k) (target Γ))
      (150*(k+1)^2) ∧
    ∀ f g : I → Bool,
      let loss := fun (H : I → I → Bool) (D : Finset ℕ) =>
        (Finset.univ.filter (fun z : I × I => H z.1 z.2 ≠ xor (target D z.1 z.2) (xor (f z.1) (g z.2)))).card
      ∃ C₀, fits C₀ ∧ (∀ D : Finset ℕ, D ⊆ Γ → loss (table C₀) D = N*D.card) ∧
        ∀ t : ℕ, t ≤ Q →
          let sets := Γ.powersetCard t
          let opt := N * min t (Q-t)
          (∀ H : I → I → Bool, opt ≤ sets.sup (loss H)) ∧
          (∃ H : I → I → Bool, sets.sup (loss H) = opt) ∧
          ∀ (l : ℕ) (w : Fin l → ℝ) (C : Fin l → PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit),
            (∀ i, 0 ≤ w i) → (∑ i, w i) = 1 → (∀ i, fits (C i)) →
            ∃ D ∈ sets,
              let err := ∑ i : Fin l, w i * (loss (table (C i)) D : ℝ)
              (opt : ℝ) ≤ err ∧ (Q < 2*t →
                ((128*(N*(Q-t))+N*(2*t-Q) : ℕ) : ℝ) < 128*err)
changed.unlocks: Separates the unrestricted and randomized budgeted worst-case error above half of a structured shift support.
changed.context: Use the complete cubic graph. Its switched distance is at least 2(Q-2), with ≤Q edits per row. Apply the square-density gate bound at v=Q-10 to force full-support loss above NQ/128. changed.title: At every gate budget a uniform cyclic choice of selector circuits attains the exact worst expected error
changed.statement:
∀ (a k B t : ℕ), 2*2^a ≤ k → t ≤ 2^a →
  let r := 2^a
  let N := 2^k
  let I := Fin r
  let X := Fin N
  let label := fun j : I => 2^(r+j.val)
  let loss := fun (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit) (D : Finset I) =>
    ((Finset.univ : Finset (X × X)).filter (fun z =>
      C.eval (PEqualNP.Represents.oneEach z.1 z.2) ≠
        xor (z.1.val.testBit (z.2.val % r)) (decide (Nat.xor z.1.val z.2.val ∈ D.image label)))).card
  let cost := fun C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit =>
    C.gates.countP (fun g => g.inputs.length == 2)
  let fits := fun C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit =>
    (∀ g ∈ C.gates, g.inputs.length ≤ 2) ∧ cost C ≤ B
  let score := fun C => (r-t)*loss C ∅ + t*loss C Finset.univ
  ∃ (base : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit) (rot : I → PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit),
    fits base ∧ (∀ C, fits C → score base ≤ score C) ∧
    (∀ s, fits (rot s) ∧ cost (rot s) = cost base ∧ (rot s).gates.length = base.gates.length ∧
      ∀ D : Finset I, loss (rot s) D = loss base (D.image (fun j => j+s))) ∧
    (∀ D : Finset I, D.card = t → (∑ s : I, loss (rot s) D) = score base) ∧
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (p : Fin n → ℝ) (circs : Fin n → PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit),
      (∀ i, 0 ≤ p i) → (∑ i, p i) = 1 → (∀ i, fits (circs i)) →
      ∃ D : Finset I, D.card = t ∧ (score base : ℝ) ≤
        (r : ℝ) * ∑ i : Fin n, p i * (loss (circs i) D : ℝ)
changed.unlocks: Computes the budgeted worst expected loss from two deterministic error counts on a high-coordinate selector family.
changed.context: Each flipped matching has N cells. A toggle corrects its existing base errors and creates errors on its remaining cells. Averaging a t-set gives W/r since each index appears with probability t/r. Minimize the natural W, using any raw output as a feasible circuit. Rotate the r unused name bits on both banks, renaming raw operands and any raw output but fixing gate indices and missing reads. This preserves the selector and cycles the matchings. Uniform rotations give exactly the same mean for every t-set. Average any competing mixture over the t-sets.

changed.title: Budgeted selector circuits realize every dyadic coin pattern with a sharp support requirement within the specified circuit family
changed.statement:
∀ (a k : ℕ), 6 ≤ a → 2*2^a ≤ k → ∀ J : Finset (Fin a),
  let r := 2^a
  let N := 2^k
  let I := Fin r
  let X := Fin N
  let q := 2^J.card
  let L := N/(128*r)
  let marked := (Finset.univ : Finset I).filter (fun j => ∀ h ∈ J, j.val.testBit h.val = false)
  let coins := (Finset.univ : Finset I).filter (fun s =>
    ∀ h : Fin a, s.val.testBit h.val = true → h ∈ J)
  let label := fun j : I => 2^(r+j.val)
  let loss := fun (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit) (D : Finset I) =>
    ((Finset.univ : Finset (X × X)).filter (fun z =>
      C.eval (PEqualNP.Represents.oneEach z.1 z.2) ≠
        xor (z.1.val.testBit (z.2.val % r)) (decide (Nat.xor z.1.val z.2.val ∈ D.image label)))).card
  let E := L*marked.card
  ∃ rot : I → PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit,
    (∀ s, (∀ g ∈ (rot s).gates, g.inputs.length ≤ 2) ∧
      16*((rot s).gates.countP (fun g => g.inputs.length == 2)) ≤ 33*N ∧
      ∀ D : Finset I, loss (rot s) D + 2*L*((D.image (fun j => j+s)) ∩ marked).card = N*D.card+E) ∧
    coins.card = q ∧ q*E = N/128 ∧
    (∀ D : Finset I, r*(∑ s ∈ coins, loss (rot s) D) + q*2*D.card*E = q*r*(N*D.card+E)) ∧
    ∀ t : ℕ, 0 < t → t < r → ∀ p : I → ℝ, (∀ s, 0 ≤ p s) → (∑ s, p s) = 1 →
      (∀ D : Finset I, D.card = t →
        (r : ℝ)*(∑ s : I, p s * (loss (rot s) D : ℝ)) + 2*(t : ℝ)*(E : ℝ) ≤
          (r : ℝ)*((N*t+E : ℕ) : ℝ)) →
      q ≤ ((Finset.univ : Finset I).filter (fun s => 0 < p s)).card

changed.context: Group raw names to compute the bare selector in at most 2N+2*2^r+4r binary gates. Mark L cells on each chosen matching with one AND per cell, an OR tree and a final XOR using a binary MOD and unary NOT. All cells are distinct. The extra cost fits the allowance. Rotate unused name bits for the other circuits. Each loss is Nt+E minus twice the captured marks. Swapping one index forces every translated expected mark count equal at the optimal mean. Sibling score sums differ exactly at levels in J. The dyadic support criterion gives the lower bound and the fair coins.

changed.title: The support-covering upper bound for binary polynomial calculus degree (known result rebuilt)
changed.statement:
∀ (n r : ℕ) (F : Set (PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause (Fin n))), 0 < r → r ≤ n →
  (∀ E ∈ F, Finset.card E ≤ r+1) → ¬ PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Satisfiable F →
  (∀ S : Finset (Fin n), S.card = r → ∃ C : PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause (Fin n), (C.image Prod.fst) ⊆ S ∧
    (∀ i : Fin n, ¬ ((i, true) ∈ C ∧ (i, false) ∈ C)) ∧
    PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.PCDerivable (PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.cnfSystem F) r (PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.clausePoly C)) →
    PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.PCRefutable (PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.cnfSystem F) (r+1)

changed.context: Reduce every degree-r monomial to lower degree, using a Boolean axiom for repeated variables or a supported clause for squarefree monomials. changed.title: For positive address and border parameters a tagged selector forces a squared deficit in the two-slot gate budget
changed.statement:
∀ (k a d : ℕ), (0 < a ∧ 2^a ≤ k ∧ 0 < d ∧ 2*d+1 ≤ k) →
  let N := 2^k
  let m := k-d
  let h := 2^m
  let δ := 2^(m-2)
  let low := fun (i j : Fin N) =>
    ((Finset.range m).filter (fun l => i.val.testBit l && j.val.testBit l)).card
  let cross := fun (i j : Fin N) => ((Finset.range d).filter (fun l =>
    i.val.testBit (m+l) && j.val.testBit 0 && j.val.testBit (l+1))).card
  let tag := fun (left right : Fin N) => (low left right + cross left right + cross right left)%2 == 1
  let r := 2^a
  let G := fun (x y : Fin N) => if x.val < h ∨ y.val < h then tag x y
    else x.val.testBit (y.val % r)
  PEqualNP.Represents.HasLitSize (k+k) (PEqualNP.Represents.adjFun (k := k) (l := k) G)
    (3*(r-1)+8*k+16*d+8) ∧
  ∀ (f g : Fin N → Bool) (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit),
    (∀ gate ∈ C.gates, gate.inputs.length ≤ 2) →
    let e := (Finset.univ.filter (fun p : Fin N × Fin N =>
      C.eval (PEqualNP.Represents.oneEach p.1 p.2) ≠

changed.unlocks: An exploration unit: it turns a construction we computed into a statement the checker accepted, one cell of the look at what a NOT gate does on small graphs.
changed.sketch: We hold a computed construction of 6 gates for this graph in which every NOT gate reads an input wire; its least AND/OR size is 7. An exploration unit: produce the gate list (wires 0 up: left vertices, right vertices, then the gates) and the decide proof on the promise inputs. Only a circuit counts here: no proof of the opposite is asked or credited. A NOT of an input equals the OR of the other lines of its side, so start from an AND/OR circuit and trade such an OR for one NOT.

changed.title: Known result rebuilt. A binary polynomial of degree at most d that is nonzero somewhere is nonzero on at least a 2^(-d) share of all points
changed.statement:

changed.unlocks: Turns a binary polynomial degree bound into a lower bound on the support of its evaluation function.
changed.context: Induct on n. Reduce p to multilinear form, which does not raise degree. Write p = q + x r with x the last variable. If r is zero as a function, use q in one fewer variable. If one slice is zero, the other equals r up to sign and induction at d - 1 applies. If both are nonzero, add the two bounds. Allow 90 to 180 minutes.

changed.context: Count the live fork and use the two-profile lemma. Opposite singleton readouts occur in each bank. If the shared corner is one, the two switching columns must pass through the sole NOT. Their outer monotone readout D(w,z) has D(0,1)=1 and D(1,0)=0, hence equals z, precluding opposite changes in w. At corner zero the four controls bypass the NOT. At w=1 both high-only controls suffice separately, so their paths meet at OR. At w=0 neither suffices and their pair cannot suffice. changed.title: A tight one-hot circuit containing a NOT factors through one monotone bit and at least two outside inputs
changed.statement:
∀ (n m : Nat) (A : Fin n → Fin m → Bool), 3 ≤ n → 3 ≤ m →
  let rowLE := fun i k : Fin n => ∀ j, A i j = true → A k j = true
  let colLE := fun j l : Fin m => ∀ i, A i j = true → A i l = true
  let rc := fun i k : Fin n => rowLE i k ∨ rowLE k i
  let cc := fun j l : Fin m => colLE j l ∨ colLE l j
  Function.Injective A → Function.Injective (fun j i => A i j) →
  (∀ i, ∃ k, ¬ rc i k) → (∀ j, ∃ l, ¬ cc j l) →
  ∀ C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit,
  PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C → PEqualNP.Represents.Represents A C →
  C.size ≤ n + m - 1 →
  (∃ gate ∈ C.gates, gate.op = PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.not) →
  ∃ (r : Fin n) (c : Fin m) (S : Finset (Fin n)) (T : Finset (Fin m))
    (W : Finset (Fin n) → Finset (Fin m) → Bool)
    (K : Finset (Fin n) → Finset (Fin m) → Bool → Bool),
    r ∉ S ∧ c ∉ T ∧ 2 ≤ S.card + T.card ∧
    (∀ i ∈ S, rc r i) ∧ (∀ j ∈ T, cc c j) ∧
    (∀ l l' q q', l ⊆ l' → q ⊆ q' → W l q = true → W l' q' = true) ∧
    ∀ i j, let x : Finset (Fin n) := {i}
           let y : Finset (Fin m) := {j}
           A i j = K (x ∩ S) (y ∩ T) (W ((x \ S).erase r) ((y \ T).erase c))

changed.context: Prune to the output and count operand positions. Distinct profiles allow one omitted input per bank. changed.title: Nonlinear raw-key questions for exact and partial recovery of guarded two-round outputs
changed.statement:
∀ (k : Nat), 0 < k → ∀ constant : Nat → Fin (2 ^ k),
  let rot := fun (s word : Nat) =>
    ((word <<< (s % k)) ||| (word >>> (k - s % k))) % 2 ^ k
  let step := fun (word : Nat) =>
    (List.range k).foldl (fun acc cell =>
      acc ||| ((xor (word.testBit cell)
        (!(word.testBit ((cell + 1) % k)) && word.testBit ((cell + 2) % k))).toNat <<< cell)) 0
  let state := fun (row rounds key : Nat) =>
    (List.range rounds).foldl (fun prev tick =>
      step (prev ^^^ rot 1 prev ^^^ rot (k - 1) prev) ^^^ rot (2 * tick) key ^^^
        (constant (tick + 1)).val) (rot 1 key ^^^ row)
  let injected := fun (round key pos : Nat) =>
    xor ((rot (2 * (round - 1)) key).testBit (pos % k))
      ((constant round).val.testBit (pos % k))
  let bit := fun (row round key pos : Nat) => (state row round key).testBit (pos % k)
  ∀ (m : Nat) (starts : Fin m → Nat),
  Function.Injective (fun z : Fin m × Fin 12 => (starts z.1+z.2.val) % k) →
  let good := fun (row ref : Fin (2^k)) (p : Nat) =>
    let old := fun (j : Nat) => bit row.val 0 ref.val (p+j)
    let first := fun (j : Nat) => bit row.val 1 ref.val (p+j)
    let τ := xor (xor (old 6) (old 7)) (old 8)
    let α := xor (xor (xor (old 5) (old 6)) (old 7)) (injected 1 ref.val (p+6))
    let β := xor τ (injected 1 ref.val (p+7))
    τ = false ∧ xor (xor (first 3) (first 4)) (first 5) = true ∧
      xor (first 4) (first 5) = !α ∧ first 4 = β
  ∀ (row ref : Fin (2^k)), (∀ i, good row ref (starts i)) →
  ∀ pin : Finset (Fin k),
  (∀ i (j : Fin 9), ∃ z ∈ pin, z.val = (starts i+j.val) % k) →
  (∀ i (j : Fin 3), ∀ z ∈ pin, z.val ≠ (starts i+9+j.val) % k) →
  let K := Fin (2^k)
  let bitOf := fun (q : K) (i : Fin k) => q.val.testBit i.val
  let par := fun (n : Nat) => n % 2 == 1
  let fiber := (Finset.univ : Finset K).filter (fun keyWord =>
    ∀ z ∈ pin, bit row.val 0 keyWord.val z.val = bit row.val 0 ref.val z.val)
  let deg := fun (u : Nat) (f : K → Bool) =>
    ∃ terms : Finset (Finset (Fin k)), (∀ mon ∈ terms, mon.card ≤ u) ∧
      ∀ key, f key = par ((terms.filter (fun mon => ∀ j ∈ mon, bitOf key j = true)).card)
  let run := fun (steps : Nat) (ask : Nat → Nat → K → Bool) (x : K) =>
    (List.range steps).foldl (fun past levelId => past + ((ask levelId past x).toNat <<< levelId)) 0
  let out := fun (input : K) (i : Fin m) => bit row.val 2 input.val (starts i+5)
  (∀ (b d L : Nat) (ask : Nat → Nat → K → Bool) (leaf : Nat → Fin L → Fin m → K → Bool),
    (∀ (u : Fin d) (path : Nat), deg b (ask u.val path)) →
    (∀ path a i, deg 2 (leaf path a i)) →
    let hit := fiber.filter (fun sample => ∃ a, ∀ i, leaf (run d ask sample) a i sample = out sample i)
    let count := (Finset.range (m+1)).sum (fun filled =>
      if filled < L*(b*d+1) then Nat.choose m filled * 7^(m-filled) else 0)
    8^m * hit.card ≤ fiber.card * count ∧
    (hit = fiber → m+1 ≤ L*2^d ∧ m < L*(b*d+1))) ∧
  ∀ a : Nat, 1 ≤ a → a ≤ 3 →
    let size := 2^a-1
    let steps := a*(m/size) + Nat.clog 2 (m % size+1)
    ∃ (choose : Nat → Nat → K → Bool) (pred : Nat → Fin m → K → Bool),
      (∀ (level : Fin steps) (path : Nat), deg (2^(a-1)) (choose level.val path)) ∧
      (∀ path i, deg 2 (pred path i)) ∧
      ∀ x ∈ fiber, ∀ i, pred (run steps choose x) i x = out x i

changed.title: A monotone shared bit leaves exactly two inside rows and columns and behaves there as OR
changed.statement:
∀ (n m : Nat) (A : Fin n → Fin m → Bool)
    (r : Fin n) (c : Fin m) (S : Finset (Fin n)) (T : Finset (Fin m))
    (W : Finset (Fin n) → Finset (Fin m) → Bool)
    (K : Finset (Fin n) → Finset (Fin m) → Bool → Bool),
  let rowLE := fun i k : Fin n => ∀ j, A i j = true → A k j = true
  let colLE := fun j l : Fin m => ∀ i, A i j = true → A i l = true
  let rc := fun i k : Fin n => rowLE i k ∨ rowLE k i
  let cc := fun j l : Fin m => colLE j l ∨ colLE l j
  Function.Injective A → Function.Injective (fun j i => A i j) →
  r ∉ S → c ∉ T → (∀ i ∈ S, rc r i) → (∀ j ∈ T, cc c j) →
  (∃ u, ¬ rc r u) → (∃ v, ¬ cc c v) →
  (∀ l l' q q', l ⊆ l' → q ⊆ q' → W l q = true → W l' q' = true) →
  (∀ i j, let x : Finset (Fin n) := {i}
          let y : Finset (Fin m) := {j}
          A i j = K (x ∩ S) (y ∩ T) (W ((x \ S).erase r) ((y \ T).erase c))) →
  ∃ (u : Fin n) (v : Fin m), ¬ rc r u ∧ ¬ cc c v ∧
    (∀ i, i ∉ S ↔ i = r ∨ i = u) ∧ (∀ j, j ∉ T ↔ j = c ∨ j = v) ∧
    K ∅ ∅ false = K ∅ ∅ true ∧ W ∅ ∅ = false ∧ W {u} ∅ = true ∧
    W ∅ {v} = true ∧ W {u} {v} = true
changed.unlocks: Determines which inside inputs can be distinguished through a shared monotone bit.
changed.context: Off the outside columns, suppose the ordinary readout is identity or negation. Every outside row copies the omitted inner row. An oppositely signed readout there makes complementary comparable profiles, forcing constancy. Thus the omitted column compares with all columns, impossible. With a constant ordinary readout, inside rows agree on inside columns and on outside columns depend only on their one inner bit with no column input. Injectivity permits two profiles; incomparability requires both. Transpose for columns. Monotonicity fixes the four inner bits.

changed.title: Which positions of named symbols can a low-degree polynomial distinguish on permutations?
changed.statement:
∀ (m h : Nat), 2 ≤ m →
  let K := ZMod 2
  let U := Fin m → K
  let H := Fin h → K
  let I := U × H
  let J := I × (Fin m ⊕ Fin h)
  let bit := fun (p : Equiv.Perm I) (j : J) =>
    Sum.elim (p j.1).1 (p j.1).2 j.2
  ∀ f : (H → I) → K,
    (∃ T : Finset (Finset J), (∀ mon ∈ T, mon.card ≤ m) ∧
      ∀ p : Equiv.Perm I, (∑ mon ∈ T, ∏ j ∈ mon, bit p j) =
        f (fun t => p.symm (0,t))) ↔
    (∃ (c : K) (z : I → K), ∀ v : H → I, Function.Injective v →
      f v = c + ∑ t : H, z (v t))
changed.unlocks: Identifies every degree-bounded lookup on the named symbol positions using permutation inputs alone.
changed.context: Translate every prefix by each m-bit word while fixing all suffixes. Summing a polynomial of degree at most m gives a constant independent of the base permutation. A surviving monomial must supply all m distinct shift bits, using every factor. The ordered positions of the zero-prefix symbols range over the blocks of an arbitrary equipartition. Apply the additive characterization. Conversely the zero-prefix indicator at each position is a product of m affine bits, so summing the weighted indicators realizes the table.
